title: Microglial Metabolic Reprogramming Regulated by HIF-1α/HK2 Positive Feedback Inhibits Adult Hippocampal Neurogenesis in Diabetes-Associated Cognitive Dysfunction.
abstract: Diabetes-associated cognitive dysfunction (DACD) is a significant complication with few effective treatments and unclear underlying mechanism. The aim of this study was to investigate how hyperglycemia disrupts adult hippocampal neurogenesis (AHN) through metabolic-immune interactions, seeking to identify potential treatment targets for DACD. DACD models were developed using db/db mice or streptozotocin-induced mice, and their cognitive function was assessed through behavioral tests. Next, we integrated multi-omics analyses (transcriptomic, single-cell, and lactylome profiling) with metabolic studies in BV2 cells exposed to diabetic conditions. Pharmacological modulators (3-BP, C646, TSA) were used to clarify the underlying mechanisms. The mice with DACD demonstrated cognitive deficits, impaired AHN, and activation of hippocampal microglia. Transcriptomic analysis revealed glycolysis as the primary dysregulated pathway. Mechanistically, hyperglycemia/AGEs induced glycolytic reprogramming and increased lactate levels, which promoted HIF-1α lactylation at lysine residues-a modification catalyzed by p300 and opposed by histone deacetylases. This posttranslational modification was associated with HIF-1α stabilisation and with enhanced transcriptional occupancy at the HK2 promoter. This established a self-amplifying feedback loop, perpetuating microglial activation and disrupting the blood-brain barrier via CXCL10 secretion, which led to CD8+ T-cell infiltration. Systemic administration of the glycolytic inhibitor 3-BP disrupted the pathogenic circuit, thereby normalizing metabolism, attenuating neuroinflammation, and restoring cognitive function. HIF-1α lactylation is associated with HIF-1α stabilisation, acting as a potential metabolic-epigenetic mechanism that links glycolytic flux to sustained microglial activation, neuroinflammation and impaired AHN in DACD. Pharmacological inhibition of this axis attenuated neuroinflammation and improved cognitive outcomes in our model, suggesting a candidate therapeutic strategy for DACD.

E3 ubiquitin ligases MKRN1/2 and RNF214 are required for efficient stress granule clearance.
abstract: Stress granules (SGs) are dynamic biomolecular condensates formed by proteins, RNAs, and ribonucleoprotein complexes in response to various forms of stress. Although SGs play a protective role in stress adaptation, impaired SG disassembly during stress recovery has been implicated in aging and neurodegeneration. The efficient clearance of SGs requires the ubiquitin-proteasome system, but specific E3 ubiquitin ligases (E3s) involved remain poorly characterized. In this study, we identify RING finger protein 214 (RNF214) and the Makorins MKRN1 and MKRN2 as key regulators of SG turnover. All three E3s associate with arsenite- and heat-induced SGs, and their depletion compromises SG clearance. Loss of MKRN1/2, but not RNF214, is linked to impaired proteasomal protein degradation: It disrupts K48-linked polyubiquitylation of SGs, prevents 26S proteasome recruitment to SGs, results in the accumulation of misfolded proteins at SGs, and generates persistent SGs that are targets for granulophagy. Co-depletion of MKRN1/2 and RNF214 causes an additive SG clearance defect, indicating that these E3s control SG disassembly through distinct, proteasome-dependent and -independent functions, respectively.

title: Author Correction: Serine protease inhibitor A3 is a soluble SIRPα ligand that suppresses inflammation and antitumor immunity.
Gene discovery and pleiotropic architecture of multidimensional pain in a genome-wide association study of >1.2 million individuals.
abstract: Chronic pain is highly prevalent worldwide, yet its genetic architecture remains to be fully elucidated. Here we leveraged data from 1,235,695 European-ancestry individuals across three biobanks. In a meta-analytic genome-wide association study of multidimensional pain (MP), we identified 343 independent loci, 92 of which were new pain associations. Sex-specific meta-analyses revealed 115 independent loci (12 of which were new) among males (n = 583,066) and 12 loci (2 of which were new) among females (n = 241,266). Multi-omic gene prioritization analyses highlighted 490 genes associated with MP through their effects on brain-specific and blood-specific regulation. Mendelian randomization analyses showed causal associations between MP and psychiatric disorders, substance use disorders and C-reactive protein levels. MP variants also showed pleiotropic associations with several brain imaging-derived phenotypes. This study expands our knowledge of the genetics of pain and its pathogenesis, highlighting the importance of its pleiotropy with multiple disorders and elucidating its multi-omic pathophysiology.

title: Mapping mammalian placental formation and implantation transitions with single-cell transcriptomics and live imaging.
abstract: Implantation remains the most inaccessible stage of mammalian development. Consequently, we know remarkably little about how the embryo coordinates the cellular transitions that establish the body plan and initiate placental formation, despite this being the period when most pregnancies are lost. Here we combine single-cell transcriptomics, live imaging and functional experiments to define these transitions at cellular resolution. Our results identify an intermediate state bridging naive and primed pluripotency in the embryonic lineage, trace anterior-posterior axis specification origins in the extraembryonic endoderm, and reveal trophectoderm bifurcation into distinct placental progenitors. Strikingly, we find that the placenta arises from two sources: the classically recognized polar trophectoderm and a previously unrecognized population of mural trophectoderm that migrates from the polar-mural border. Human mural trophectoderm shows similar region-specific behaviour and may include invasive-trophoblast-biased progenitors. These findings open new directions for improving stem-cell-derived embryo models and uncovering the early determinants of pregnancy success.

title: The optogenetic tool ASAP acutely inhibits autophagy.
abstract: Autophagy, a conserved recycling process, manages intracellular quality control to mitigate stress. To determine the rapid effects of autophagy perturbation, we developed an optogenetic tool to rapidly inhibit autophagy, termed ASAP. Our approach leverages light-induced proteolytic cleavage to selectively inhibit autophagy within 5 min of light exposure, providing a precise and dynamic approach to study autophagy regulation. Proteomic profiling with ASAP revealed the most tightly regulated autophagy substrates along with previously unidentified substrates, including nuclear pore complex proteins. Of note, autophagy regulates quality control of cytoplasmic complexes of nucleoporins via specific LC3-interacting regions, sparing nuclear pore complex proteins embedded in the nuclear envelope. Upon rapid autophagy inhibition, incomplete nucleoporin complexes accumulate and instead of undergoing autophagic degradation, cytoplasmic nucleoporin complexes aggregate in processing bodies (P bodies). Using ASAP, we demonstrate rapid and specific inhibition of autophagy, revealing that nuclear pore complex proteins are tightly regulated autophagy substrates.

title: Altered heart-brain coupling in awake patients with isolated REM sleep behaviour disorder.
abstract: Isolated REM sleep behaviour disorder (iRBD) represents a prodromal stage of alpha-synucleinopathies, frequently preceding Parkinson's disease and dementia with Lewy bodies. Beyond the characteristic sleep disturbances, alterations in brain-body coupling, reflecting neural peripheral physiological interactions, have yet to be determined. Using whole-night polysomnography, we quantified brain-body coupling via heartbeat evoked potentials (HEPs) across wakefulness, NREM, and REM sleep. Individuals with iRBD (n = 13) were compared with healthy controls (n = 23), alongside analyses of ECG-derived features. During wakefulness, iRBD patients showed altered HEPs over frontal regions between 305 and 445 ms after the R-peak. No significant group differences were observed during NREM or REM sleep, and HEP amplitude alterations were not explained by ECG differences. These diurnal HEP changes may represent a novel quantitative biomarker for iRBD during wakefulness and, in the future, could serve as a marker for phenoconversion to alpha-synucleinopathy.

title: A novel Porphyra enzymatic hydrolysate modulates gut microbiota and enhances propionate production to alleviate osteoarthritis.
abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a global health challenge with limited nutritional and therapeutic options. Porphyra, an edible-medicinal red alga rich in bioactive compounds with gut-modulating properties, yet remains underutilized as most products are low-value preliminary processed goods. Enzymatic hydrolysis represents a promising strategy to improve the processing and functional utilization of Porphyra. Nevertheless, the chondroprotective effects of Porphyra-derived enzymatic hydrolysates and their potential involvement in the gut-joint axis have not been established. In this study, a Porphyra enzymatic hydrolysate (PEPP) was developed by using food-grade porphyranase combined with neutral protease, which exhibited a higher liquefaction rate than protease-only hydrolysate (PEP) and contained oligo-porphyran and peptides. Oral administration of PEPP reduced cartilage destruction, and improved chondrocyte metabolism in OA mice. Mechanistically, PEPP reshaped gut microbiota, promoted propionate production, and propionate attenuated OA progression by upregulating TNFAIP3 to inhibit NF-κB pathway, thereby suppressing chondrocyte catabolism. These findings indicate PEPP as a functional ingredient derived from Porphyra, and support its development as a dietary strategy for promoting joint health through the gut-joint axis.

title: Persistent impairment of spatial hearing and neural binaural interaction after "temporary" noise-induced hearing loss.
abstract: Many people have suprathreshold auditory processing difficulties despite normal audiometric thresholds, referred to as "hidden hearing loss." Such difficulties are widely thought to originate from pathology of the inner hair cell ribbon synapse (cochlear synaptopathy) following noise-exposure-induced temporary threshold shifts. This pathology impairs the temporally-precise sound encoding necessary for spatial hearing, but direct evidence in primates, human or nonhuman, is lacking. Here, we show in macaques of both sexes that noise-exposure-induced temporary threshold shifts produced long-lasting alterations in synaptic morphology without synapse loss, and persistent spatial hearing deficits up to 11 months post-exposure, despite recovery of audiometric thresholds. These deficits were accompanied by a reduction in a neurophysiological measure of binaural processing - the binaural interaction component of the auditory brainstem response. Together, these findings provide evidence, in primates, that noise exposure disrupts spatial hearing and binaural neural circuit function without loss of hair cells or synapses.

title: Social determinants of health and the exposome shape aging and dementia across global populations.
abstract: Social determinants of health, the conditions in which people are born, grow, live, work and age, shape brain aging and dementia. Yet evidence is dominated by Global North populations and often relies on single indicators (for example, education or income), limiting risk characterization and generalizability across settings. This Perspective provides a global, integrative overview of multidimensional, multilevel and life-course approaches to social determinants of health and exposome research in brain health. We examine composite indices and social-exposomal factors, their need for harmonization, contextual adaptation and local validation, and biological embedding through stress-related, inflammatory, metabolic, vascular and epigenetic pathways. We also discuss interactions with genetic susceptibility and the analytical challenges of modeling cumulative, time-varying and nonlinear exposures. These advances require feasible, policy-relevant implementation in resource-constrained settings. Moving beyond static, single-domain proxies towards context-sensitive measures and multilevel designs can improve risk characterization and support more equitable, globally relevant strategies for dementia prevention and precision public health.

title: Body mass regulation in humans is associated with dopamine synthesis capacity and dopamine receptor profile measured with positron emission tomography.
abstract: The widespread and increasing prevalence of excess body mass represents a major public health concern and has been hypothesized to involve dysfunction of the dopaminergic reward system. However, a detailed, systems-level understanding of interactions between the dopamine system and body mass regulation in humans has been elusive. To address this knowledge gap, we employed positron emission tomography (PET) to directly measure presynaptic dopamine synthesis capacity (with [18F]-FDOPA) and dopamine receptor availability (D1 and D2/3 receptors with [11C]-NNC112 and [18F]-Fallypride, respectively) in 117 individuals with body mass index (BMI) values ranging from normal to moderately obese. We found that elevated BMI was associated with heightened dopamine synthesis capacity in the midbrain and hypothalamus, key regions for homeostatic appetite control, as well as with lower D2/3 receptor availability in the midbrain, where D2 receptors play an important role in the autoregulation of striatal dopamine release. Moreover, we found that the presence and rate of weight gain in the 1-2 years prior to scanning was associated with increased presynaptic dopamine synthesis capacity in the ventral striatum and midbrain, important components of the reward network. These data suggest that upregulation of body mass beyond the normal range is related to increased dopamine synthesis capacity in reward- and homeostatic-related regions coupled with blunted autoregulation.

title: Trapped in time: a collapse of temporal irreversibility and remodeling of causal connectivity in major depressive disorder.
abstract: Healthy brain dynamics evolve in the direction far from thermodynamic equilibrium. The temporal asymmetry nature recently has been described in several normal and pathological brain states. However, whether the temporal asymmetry of spontaneous brain activity is affected by Major Depression Disorders (MDD) remains unknown. Resting-state fMRI data from 178 MDD patients and 205 healthy controls (HCs) were analyzed. We quantified temporal irreversibility (IR) by comparing forward and backward time series through time-shifted correlations using a sliding-windowed approach, constructed IR-based functional hierarchy, identified IR substates through k-means clustering, and estimated effective connectivity among key IR impaired regions using spectral Dynamical Causal Modeling (DCM). Associations with Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAMD) scores were further examined. MDD patients exhibited globally reduced IR, particularly within the default mode (DMN), attention (ATN), and sensorimotor (SM) networks, and across eight key regions. Functional hierarchy were significantly flattened in these systems. Clustering revealed two IR substates, characterized by globally high IR (State1) or low IR (State2). MDD patients occupied State2 more dominantly, exhibited longer dwell time, and transitioned into it more frequently. DCM revealed strengthened excitatory drive within the DMN and altered cross-network influences in MDD. DCM for subgroups further demonstrated progressive remodeling of causal connections across different severity levels. We demonstrate a pervasive shift for MDD toward equilibrium dynamics and network-specific causal pathologies. Our study provides a multi-faceted characterization of MDD-related brain dynamic alterations.

title: Activation of GLP-1 receptors suppresses pathological defensive aggression via DMPAG in mice.
abstract: Defensive aggression is an evolutionarily conserved instinct, and its dysregulation represents a common behavioral manifestation in multiple psychiatric disorders. Although glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) are widely used for metabolic diseases, their role in aggressive behavior remains unclear. Here, we employed behavioral assays, chemogenetics, immunofluorescence, pharmacological manipulations, and metabolomics to investigate the regulatory effects of GLP-1RA on defensive aggression in mice. Acute intracerebroventricular administration of GLP-1RA significantly suppressed defensive aggression without affecting locomotor activity or time spent in the center of the open field. c-Fos immunofluorescence indicated that this effect was associated with reduced neuronal activity in the dorsomedial periaqueductal gray (DMPAG). Chemogenetic activation of DMPAG neurons reversed the suppressive effect of GLP-1RA on defensive aggression, supporting a key regulatory role of this region. In a social isolation (SI) induced pathological aggression model, GLP-1RA alleviated excessive defensive aggression and modulated the metabolic state of the DMPAG. Notably, GLP-1RA restored levels of L-carnosine, a dipeptide with neuroprotective and anti-excitotoxic properties whose levels were reduced in SI mice. Carnosine infusion into the DMPAG suppressed defensive aggression in SI mice, whereas administration of the carnosine degrading enzyme CNDP2 attenuated the suppressive effect of GLP-1RA, supporting carnosine signaling as a functionally relevant downstream component. These findings identify a carnosine-associated pathway by which GLP-1RA regulates defensive aggression and highlight its therapeutic potential beyond metabolic regulation.

title: Dendritic computation bridges neuroscience and foundation models.
abstract: A prevailing view holds that although neuroscience historically inspired AI, its role in the recent evolution of AI, driven by the scaling of foundation models, is minor. We challenge this perspective by establishing a biological analogy between simplified dendritic neuron models and the attention mechanisms central to AI foundation models. We show that AI attention mechanisms bear direct mappings to internal neuronal complexities arising from dendritic organization, rather than to the mere inter-neuronal connections of simple point neurons. This re-conceptualization not only offers a neuroscience-informed perspective for understanding core AI methodologies beyond their formulation as abstract mathematical operations, but also paves the way for neuro-inspired foundation models that leverage neuroscientific insights to sustainably advance modern AI beyond scaling laws. As an example of this paradigm, we introduce a dendritic-inspired complexity framework, and design a hybrid-attention foundation model with dendritic-inspired sparse computation, which enhances memory capacity while reducing computational demands. Our model supports a 50M context window-equivalent to roughly 40 volumes of Shakespeare-demonstrating superior long-term memory capabilities. This work pioneers a paradigm that harnesses intra-neuronal dynamics to drive sustained advances in modern AI, while also offering a potential route to understanding dendritic computational mechanisms.

title: Brain-wide pathways for object identity and location are dominated by internal strategies.
abstract: It is long thought that higher-order sensory processing is divided into two specialized cortical streams that encode in parallel either the identity of an object or its location (i.e., 'what' and 'where' streams). Here, using the mouse whisker system, we demonstrate an existence of two alternating brain-wide (beyond cortex) subnetworks that are primarily driven by internal strategies, rather than external parameters. We combine simultaneous brain-wide neuronal recordings in male mice trained to identify or locate a certain stimulus. We find that mice deploy either an active search or a passive sensation strategy during task performance. These strategies respectively drive two distinct brain-wide subnetworks, frontal and posterior related to an active and passive strategy respectively. Using a computational framework, we show that the posterior subnetwork encoded additional internal strategic parameters such as trial history, the first task of the day, and training history. When discarding the dominance of the frontal subnetwork, specific areas within the posterior subnetwork encoded meaningful task information regarding object identity and location. Integrated together, these two subnetworks may comprise optimal sensory integration.

title: SLITRK2 knockdown rescues axonal and functional neuromuscular junction deficits in human iPSC-derived mutant FUS-ALS motor neurons.
abstract: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a fatal neurodegenerative disease characterized by motor neuron (MN) loss caused by early axonal and synaptic changes. However, the mechanisms underlying these changes remain incompletely understood. Here, we exploit FUS-ALS to interrogate cell compartment-specific changes in RNA expression and regulation in human induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived MN. This approach identifies compartment-specific 3' untranslated region (3'UTR) isoform expression in human healthy control MN axons. Further, it unveils altered 3' UTR isoforms in ALS in different cellular compartments in genes such as SNCA, previously linked to neurodegeneration. Expression of SLITRK2 is most strongly and consistently upregulated across multiple FUS-ALS models, and its knockdown normalizes axonal defects linked to FUS-ALS. Using a fully iPSC-derived neuromuscular microfluidics protocol, we show that SLITRK2 knockdown in FUS-ALS MN rescues neuromuscular junction (NMJ) signaling without affecting NMJ innervation or MN hypo-excitability. Our study provides insight into compartment-specific 3'UTR expression in ALS, presents a robust iNMJ-on-a-chip model, and links elevated SLITRK2 to axonal and synaptic defects in FUS-ALS.

title: Reduced manual dexterity and muscle strength relative to normative data in children and adolescents with Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease: Limited association with distal and proximal strength.
authors: de Baptista Cyntia Rogean de Jesus Alves
journal: Journal of hand therapy : official journal of the American Society of Hand Therapists
abstract: Manual dexterity, together with distal and proximal muscle strength, represents essential components of upper-limb structure and function and is associated with the performance of daily activities in youths with Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease (CMT). To compare manual dexterity and handgrip strength with normative reference values and to examine their association with distal and proximal muscle strength in children and adolescents with CMT. Cross-sectional study. The study included 39 children and adolescents with CMT (mean age 13.2 ± 4.2 years). Manual dexterity was assessed using the Nine-Hole Peg Test (NHPT), and muscle performance was evaluated through handgrip strength and isometric peak torque of elbow flexors and extensors. Age- and sex-adjusted normative reference data were used for comparison through z-score standardization. Associations were analyzed using Spearman's correlation with Benjamini-Hochberg correction for multiple comparisons. Children and adolescents with CMT showed significantly poorer manual dexterity and lower muscle strength than normative reference values. A low negative correlation was observed between NHPT and handgrip strength in the overall CMT group (ρ = -0.37, p = 0.02), whereas no evidence of correlation was found within the CMT1A or CMT_o subgroups or between manual dexterity and elbow flexor or extensor strength. Children and adolescents with CMT exhibit impaired manual dexterity and reduced muscle strength relative to normative reference values. The limited association between manual dexterity and muscle strength suggests that manual performance may depend on factors beyond maximal muscle strength.

title: Exercise is medicine: Translating exercise-induced cognitive benefits into rehabilitation practice.
journal: Journal of hand therapy : official journal of the American Society of Hand Therapists
abstract: Exercise is one of the most impactful activities we can do to support physical, cognitive, and mental health across the lifespan and within both healthy and clinical populations. There is robust evidence that exercise promotes cognitive function, enhancing our ability to plan, think, and execute goal-directed behaviours. These cognitive benefits directly support patients in rehabilitation contexts to understand, follow, and safely apply clinical recommendations. In this expert review, we provide an overview of the exercise neuroscience literature, highlighting key findings for the effects of exercise on cognition and brain health, followed by an overview of proposed mechanisms for these findings. Next, we translate these findings and offer a perspective in how they may be beneficial in rehabilitation settings, including special considerations for different populations experiencing cognitive decline. Finally, we end with a discussion of the limitations and future directions of this work, with special attention to equity, diversity, and inclusion to ensure that this knowledge remains accessible to all. Our goal is to provide clinicians and researchers with the background knowledge that will equip them with what, how, and why exercise should be part of usual care for all types of patients in rehabilitation settings.

title: Quality of life of radiologists in France: From measurement to action.
Donor Willingness and Participation in Health and Genetic Screening Within Blood Banks: A Narrative Review.
abstract: Blood banks increasingly offer additional health and genomic screening alongside routine donation, providing donors with personalized results. This review aims to assess the available evidence on donors' willingness to participate in additional screening and the behavioral outcomes following receipt of the results. We conducted a systematic search in Embase, PubMed, and Web of Science (February-March 2026) using predefined search terms and clear inclusion criteria. We identified 9 relevant studies. From the eligible studies, we selected 5 articles for review that had the highest relevance to the research questions and offered complementary perspectives across genetic, metabolic, and cardiovascular screening modalities. Donors expressed a high willingness to participate in additional screening when it was supported by trust in the blood bank and clarity about the screening's voluntary and secondary nature. Donors emphasized that receiving personal or genomic results should remain secondary to helping patients, in order to preserve the altruistic gift‑relationship that motivates donation. Behavioral actions, such as seeking care, making lifestyle changes, and discussing results with family, occurred mainly when donors received and understood their results. Clear communication and follow‑up procedures functioned as an underlying mechanism that supported both participation and appropriate action. As additional screening becomes integrated into blood donation practice, effective communication and supportive follow-up procedures are essential to promote informed participation and appropriate health-related action.

title: ERN-RITA/PReS recommendations for the diagnosis, classification, monitoring, and treatment of childhood idiopathic (primary) angiitis of the central nervous system.
abstract: Childhood central nervous system (CNS) vasculitis is a rare and serious disease for which no evidence-based consensus guidance, standardised terminology, or definitions of treatment response exist. We aimed to develop the first international recommendations for the diagnosis, classification, monitoring, and treatment of CNS vasculitis in children. Adapting the European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology standardised operating procedures, an international multidisciplinary panel of 42 experts from 15 countries was assembled through the European Reference Network on Rare Immunodeficiency, Autoinflammatory, Autoimmune and Paediatric Rheumatic Diseases, and the Paediatric Rheumatology European Society. A systematic literature review across 4 databases identified 182 eligible studies, graded per the Oxford Centre for Evidence-Based Medicine hierarchy. A modified Delphi survey (42 respondents) was followed by a 2-day face-to-face consensus conference (26 voting members; ≥70% agreement required). The panel formulated 83 consensus statements (3 overarching principles, 14 principles, and 66 recommendations) across 7 clinical domains. Of 182 included articles, 152 (83.5%) reported paediatric data; no level 1 evidence was identified. Key advances include an 8-domain nomenclature system replacing the 'primary/secondary' dichotomy with 'idiopathic/disease-associated' terminology, a paediatric-specific vessel wall imaging interpretive principle, a prospective risk-stratification model for disease progression, genome-wide sequencing as the preferred genetic testing approach, and formal definitions of remission, relapse, and refractory disease. None of these elements had been previously codified for childhood CNS vasculitis. These recommendations establish a comprehensive, evidence-graded framework for childhood CNS vasculitis. The absence of level 1 evidence across all domains points to the need for an international prospective registry and collaborative clinical trials.

Reelin Deficiency Alters the Directional Orientation, Apical Localization and Length of Primary Cilia in Principal Neurons in the Cerebral Cortex.
journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
abstract: The primary cilia of pyramidal neurons in inside-out laminated regions are oriented predominantly toward the pia, a pattern reflecting reverse soma movement during postnatal neurodevelopment. However, the mechanisms that regulate the directional cilia orientation remain unknown. Here we show that the primary cilia of neocortical pyramidal neurons in male and female mice are localized at the base of the apical dendrites and aligned distally and opposite to the axon initial segment (AIS). However, this pattern is not observed in atypical pyramidal neurons in the deep neocortex, excitatory neurons in non-laminated regions, or interneurons, where cilia are randomly positioned around the nuclei and lack preferred orientation. In Reelin-deficient mice (reeler), the directional orientation and apical location of cilia in late-born neocortical and CA1 neurons are altered. However, the initial impairments are partially corrected during early postnatal development. In contrast, Reelin deficiency disrupts the directional orientation and apical localization of primary cilia in early-born neocortical neurons and principal neurons in evolutionarily conserved laminated regions, where lack postnatal correction. Reelin deficiency also increases the cilia length in principal neurons across the cerebral cortex at a developmental stage when cilia length stabilizes in wild-type mice. In contrast, cilia elongation is not observed in interneurons, GFAP-positive astrocytes, or excitatory neurons in non-laminated regions of reeler Together, Reelin regulates the directional orientation, apical localization, and length of primary cilia in principal neurons in the cerebral cortex. This study underscores the cilium as a key apical domain, particularly prominent in late-born pyramidal neurons.Significance Statement While primary cilia are implicated in various brain disorders, their physiological functions in the postnatal brain remain poorly understood. We show that the primary cilia in pyramidal neurons are localized at the base of the apical dendrites and aligned distally and opposite to the axon initial segment (AIS), forming a prominent "cilia-at-apical and axon-at-basal" pattern. Reelin deficiency alters the directional orientation, apical localization, and length of these cilia. Interestingly, late-born pyramidal neurons exhibit partial restoration under Reelin deficiency, whereas early-born neurons and those in evolutionarily conserved cortical regions do not. These findings identify primary cilia as a crucial apical domain and reveal an unrecognized Reelin-cilia functional crosstalk, which may enhance the polarity of pyramidal neurons.

title: Disentangling the Spatiotemporal Neural Dynamics of Conflict Detection and Resolution between Lexical and Sublexical Processes in Oral Word Reading: An Intracranial SEEG Study.
journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
abstract: Object recognition relies on correspondence between whole objects and their subcomponents. When this correspondence is disrupted, accurate recognition requires detecting conflicts and inhibiting misleading subcomponent information, yet the neural basis underlying these processes remain unclear. Written language, with sublexical components that may conflict with whole words, provides an ideal testbed. Using stereo-electroencephalography (SEEG) recorded from 39 participants (both sexes) during Chinese character reading, we revealed a functional dissociation between neural systems supporting conflict detection and inhibitory control. Conflict detection was associated with β band activity in the fusiform gyrus and widespread θ and α band effects across temporal and parietal regions. Inhibitory control was associated with α and β band activity in the inferior frontal and precentral gyri. Granger causality analysis showed increased β band connectivity from conflict-processing to inhibitory-control regions under conflict conditions. These findings demonstrate that disruptions of whole-sublexical correspondence engage dissociable neural systems for conflict detection and inhibitory control, implemented through frequency- and region-specific neural oscillations and coordinated via increased information transfer from posterior to frontal regions.Significance Statement Reading often requires resolving conflicts between competing linguistic representations, yet the neural mechanisms that detect such conflicts and resolve them remain poorly understood. Using stereo-electroencephalography with millimeter-scale spatial and millisecond-scale temporal resolution, we dissociated sublexical conflict detection from inhibitory control during Chinese character reading. We show that these processes are supported by distinct low-frequency oscillatory networks and are linked through directed functional interactions. These findings move beyond traditional accounts of sublexical effects by identifying their underlying cognitive components and neural dynamics, providing a mechanistic framework for understanding how cognitive control supports fluent word recognition.

PARP1 deficiency induces aging-associated cardiac failure via activation of Akt signalling.
abstract: PARP1, a major poly-ADP-ribose transferase, plays a critical role in maintaining genomic stability, transcription, cellular energy metabolism, and cell death. In the heart, PARP1 inhibition protects cardiomyocytes against oxidative and genotoxic stress and attenuates ischemia-reperfusion injury caused by myocardial infarction. However, the role of PARP1 in aging-associated heart failure remains unexplored. In this study, we demonstrate the crucial role of PARP1 in regulating aging-associated cardiac remodelling and failure. The levels of PARP1 are down-regulated in aging mouse hearts, and PARP1 deficiency induces aging-related cardiac remodelling and contractile dysfunction in mice. The RNA-seq analysis revealed hyperactivation of Akt signalling, a major signalling pathway involved in aging, in PARP1-deficient hearts. In the heart, PARP1 deficiency spontaneously activates the Akt signalling pathway, leading to the development of aging-related cardiac hypertrophy and failure. Our findings reveal two distinct mechanisms by which PARP1 regulates Akt signalling, involving the direct interaction of PARP1 with Akt and the transcriptional regulation of phosphatases, including the expression of PTEN by PARP1. Mechanistically, PARP1 binds to the PTEN promoter and might transcriptionally promote its expression. In addition, PARP1 binds and inhibits Akt by poly-ADP-ribosylating Akt at the PH domain, which impairs Akt plasma membrane recruitment and subsequent activation. Inhibition of Akt reversed hypertrophy in PARP1-depleted cardiomyocytes and improved the contractile dysfunction in PARP1-deficient hearts. These findings reveal a previously unrecognized regulatory role for PARP1 in aging-associated cardiac failure.

title: Linking distinct contextual memories across a wide time window: temporal dynamics and neuronal co-reactivation during retrieval.
abstract: Previous studies suggest that shared hippocampal neuronal ensembles link distinct contextual memories across intervals from 5 h to 7 days. Here, we examined the temporal dynamics of linking neutral and aversive contextual memories across broader timescales and analyzed reactivation of neuronal ensembles during retrieval. Memory linking occurred across hours, days, and weeks, but not at very short or very long intervals. Linked memories showed greater observed neuronal overlap in the hippocampus and amygdala, but chance-normalized overlap did not differ significantly between groups. Memory linking was also accompanied by larger retrieval-activated populations in hippocampal CA1 and lateral and basolateral amygdala.

title: MOG-IgG optic neuritis with concurrent CASPR2 antibodies: a possible link with chronic hepatitis C.
Identification of environmental conditions favourable to Pseudo-nitzschia bloom occurrence along the Portuguese Atlantic coast using satellite-derived predictors.
abstract: Pseudo-nitzschia (Pn) diatoms pose recurrent risks to coastal ecosystems and shellfish harvesting along the Portuguese Atlantic coast, where operational forecasting of bloom occurrence can support monitoring programmes by enabling earlier and targeted management responses. Here we develop and evaluate a machine-learning framework to identify environmental conditions favourable to Pn bloom occurrence along the Portuguese Atlantic coast, using exclusively satellite-derived predictors and a validation strategy designed to closely mimic real-world forecasting conditions. Predictive models were developed for the core study region (the shellfish production zones L1-L2), a long-standing hotspot for Pn and domoic acid events, using a decade-long matched dataset (2013-2023; 1440 observations) combining sea surface temperature, an upwelling index, chlorophyll-a, and plankton functional types. Across multiple model classes and feature configurations, Pn habitat suitability proved moderately predictable. Ensemble tree-based methods achieved the strongest discrimination: Random Forest reached 0.74 ± 0.05 with environmental predictors; Extra Trees reached 0.77 ± 0.06 with biological variables added. Feature-importance analyses revealed that seasonal structure, spatial context, and lagged environmental conditions dominate model decisions, while biological indicators refine bloom likelihood within physically favourable periods. The framework demonstrates operationally relevant skill for satellite-supported HAB early-warning systems along eastern boundary upwelling coasts.

title: Discovery of domoic acid biosynthesis genes in Chaetoceros costatus expands the phylogenetic range of toxigenic diatoms.
abstract: Domoic acid (DA) is the neurotoxin responsible for amnesic shellfish poisoning (ASP) long thought to be confined to only two phylogenetically related diatom genera Pseudo-nitzschia and Nitzschia in one class Bacillariophyceae, leaving the occurrence and evolutionary origin of this trait in other diatom classes unresolved. Here we revealed homologs of DA biosynthesis (dab) genes across diverse diatom lineages through large-scale mining of Tara Oceans metatranscriptomes, suggesting that other diatom lineages may harbor sequences with similarity to DA‑biosynthetic dab genes. We identified dab genes in Chaetoceros costatus (class Mediophyceae) through genome-based screening of 281 diatom strains representing 54 diatom species from Chinese waters. The C. costatus genome encodes three of the four canonical dab genes (dabA, dabC, and dabD) but lacks dabB, which is similarly absent in the DA-producing red alga Chondria armata. Analytical validation using LC-MS/MS confirmed DA production in the C. costatus strains. Chromosome-level genome assemblies revealed haplotype-specific expansions of dabA and dabD, suggesting possible key functions in diversifying DA biosynthetic capacity. The observed phylogenetic patterns are consistent with the hypothesis of multiple horizontal gene transfer events, including a putative cross-eukaryote gene acquisition between Pseudo-nitzschia and C. costatus. These findings substantially expand the known taxonomic range of DA-producing diatoms and highlight the hidden toxin potential of ecologically dominant marine diatoms.

title: Distribution of vitamin B12, Pseudo-nitzschia and domoic acid in the Northwest Passage.
abstract: The prevalence of Harmful Algal Blooms (HAB) is increasing worldwide. In the Arctic, the domoic acid (DA) producing diatom Pseudo-nitzschia is responsible for Amnesic Shellfish Poisoning events. While laboratory studies revealed vitamin B12 auxotrophy in Pseudo-nitzschia, the link between vitamin B12 distribution, Pseudo-nitzschia abundances and DA concentration is unknown. An expedition was conducted to the Arctic, in which samples for plankton biomass, dissolved (d) and particulate (p) B12, Pseudo-nitzschia and DA were collected. Multidimensional scaling showed a separation of the stations into three main clusters, primarily driven by dB12 and pB12. dB12 was lowest in the East, ranging from 0.02 to 2.46 pmol L-1, and inversely correlated to Pseudo-nitzschia and DA. In contrast, pB12 concentrations were highest in the East ranging from 0.02-0.6 pmol L-1. The observed positive correlation of Pseudo-nitzschia with DA and pB12 suggests a demand for this micronutrient by toxigenic species. Furthermore, the high DA: Pseudo-nitzschia ratio, an indicator for the toxicity of the Pseudo-nitzschia population, correlated negatively with dB12 and pB12, suggesting that toxicity could be influenced by the availability of this vitamin. Together with the very low dB12 concentrations measured, this study highlights the potential of vitamin B12 as a limiting nutrient to artic phytoplankton populations in general and Pseudo-nitzschia in particular.

title: In Vivo-In vitro correlation of Blood-Brain barrier permeability using cryopreserved human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived brain microvascular endothelial cells.
abstract: Predicting drug permeability through the blood-brain barrier (BBB) is important for developing pharmaceuticals for the central nervous system. In this study, we evaluated whether cryopreservation affects the molecular characteristics of human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived brain microvascular endothelial cells (iBMECs) using proteomic analysis. Cryopreserved iBMECs (Cryo-iBMECs) were compared with freshly differentiated iBMECs to assess global protein expression profiles and functional characteristics. Proteomic analysis revealed a strong correlation in protein expression between iBMECs and Cryo-iBMECs (Pearson's correlation coefficient r = 0.969). We further investigated whether the permeability properties of drugs in Cryo-iBMECs correlated with in vivo drug distribution. The permeability values obtained in Cryo-iBMECs were compared with reported in vivo values in mice, rats, cynomolgus monkeys, and humans. The results indicated that apparent permeability coefficients (Papp) values in Cryo-iBMECs were highly correlated with in vivo data in humans and cynomolgus monkeys. These findings indicate that Cryo-iBMECs retain key molecular characteristics and may serve as a practical in vitro platform for evaluating human BBB drug permeability.

title: Systems pharmacology and translational insights into herbal therapeutics for schizophrenia: Mechanistic advances, network-based approaches, and future directions.
abstract: Schizophrenia (SCZ) is a complex and heterogeneous neuropsychiatric disorder that is characterized by disturbances in neurotransmission, neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, synaptic dysfunction and neurodevelopmental abnormalities. Current antipsychotic drugs mainly modulate dopaminergic signaling, thus they are not fully effective in improving negative symptoms, cognitive deficits and treatment-resistant cases. Herbal therapeutics and polyherbal formulations have been gaining attention due to their inherent polypharmacological profiles and traditional ethnomedicinal use in psychiatric disorders. This review highlights recent mechanistic insights of herbal approaches for SCZ, focusing on bioactive phytochemicals, traditional polyherbal formulations, and multi-target molecular actions. The use of recent advances in systems biology, in silico studies, and integrative tools to decode herb-compound-target-pathway interactions underlying therapeutic effects is also discussed. Experimental validation of computational predictions through neuronal cell lines, stem cell-based systems, and animal models were also discussed. This review also discusses the translational potential of integrative mechanistic approaches by framing SCZ as a network disorder and herbal formulations as systems-level modulators.

title: Phenylbutyrate-Derived Nitric Oxide Donor Attenuates Renal Fibrosis through the Extracellular Matrix Degradation Pathway.
abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a major global health burden for which no curative therapy has been established. Decreased bioavailability of nitric oxide (NO) has been implicated in the pathogenesis and progression of CKD. In this study, we investigated the therapeutic potential of NPB, a novel NO donor independently synthesized by our group, in experimental CKD. In an adenine-induced CKD mouse model, NPB administration suppressed serum creatinine and blood urea nitrogen (BUN) to control levels, and Masson's trichrome staining revealed marked attenuation of renal fibrosis. In cultured renal fibroblasts, NPB significantly inhibited transforming growth factor-β1 (TGF-β1)-induced expression of fibronectin and α-smooth muscle actin (α-SMA). Importantly, OH-PB, a non-NO-donating derivative of NPB, showed no beneficial effects in either the in vivo or in vitro. Notably, NPB significantly reduced fibronectin expression even after fibrosis had been induced by TGF-β1 stimulation, an effect not reproduced by TGF-β receptor antagonists. Mechanistically, NPB had little effect on Smad2/3 phosphorylation, the central signaling cascade downstream of TGF-β. Instead, the anti-fibrotic effect of NPB on established fibronectin expression was partially attenuated by the matrix metalloproteinase (MMP) inhibitor doxycycline. Therefore, NPB is a promising therapeutic candidate for CKD that may act by promoting clearance of accumulated extracellular matrix.

title: Arid1b haploinsufficiency weakens excitatory synaptic input to inhibitory interneurons beginning during early development.
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) presents with diverse cognitive and behavioral abnormalities that begin during early development and persist into adulthood. Although the circuit mechanisms remain unclear, recent work suggests pathology in inhibitory interneurons (INs) plays a crucial role. Neocortical and hippocampal INs are generated from a common progenitor pool during embryogenesis and develop into similar major subtypes in both brain structures. Thus, dysfunction of ASD risk genes in IN progenitors may broadly impact neural circuit function. Here, we used transgenic mice to conditionally knockout one copy of the ASD risk gene Arid1b from the progenitors of parvalbumin-expressing fast-spiking (PV-FS) INs, which provide perisomatic inhibition to control spike timing, and somatostatin-expressing non-fast-spiking (SST-NFS) INs, which inhibit dendrites to control synaptic integration and plasticity. We then investigated the physiology of their synaptic connections with excitatory pyramidal cells (PCs) in slices of neocortex and CA1 hippocampus from both neonatal and adolescent mice. Surprisingly, excitatory synapses from PCs to INs were weakened throughout development in both brain regions but inhibitory synapses from INs to PCs were normal. During early development, we found that weak excitatory drive to INs impaired the generation of spontaneous network events that contribute to circuit maturation. During later development, excitatory synapses to SST-NFS INs remained weak in both neocortex and CA1, which is expected to impair their participation in canonical inhibitory circuits necessary for proper encoding of sensory and spatial information by PCs. Our data show that impaired IN excitation is an important mechanism underlying circuit deficits in Arid1b haploinsufficiency.

title: Editorial: Using Early Improvement to Guide Antipsychotic Treatment in Adolescent Schizophrenia.
journal: Journal of the American Academy of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry

title: Sympathetic neuroeffector remodeling and cardiomyocyte ferroptosis in heart failure: A stage- and compartment-specific framework for β-adrenergic/cAMP signaling.
abstract: Heart failure is characterized by sympathetic remodeling, altered myocardial adrenergic responsiveness, and cardiomyocyte injury, with ferroptosis emerging as a potential contributor to adverse cardiac remodeling. This review proposes a dynamic "sympathetic-ferroptosis continuum" within a "nerve terminal-cardiomyocyte" dual-compartment framework linking cardiac sympathetic dysfunction, β1-adrenergic receptor (β1-AR)/cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP) signaling, and cardiomyocyte ferroptosis susceptibility. Sustained sympathetic drive can coexist with altered norepinephrine (NE) homeostasis at cardiac nerve terminals and myocardial β1-AR desensitization, creating a functional mismatch between sympathetic activity and myocardial signaling responsiveness. At sympathetic nerve terminals, altered β1-AR/cAMP signaling may influence tyrosine hydroxylase-dependent NE synthesis and synapsin 1/RIM1α-associated vesicle mobilization and release, alongside changes in NE transporter-mediated reuptake. In cardiomyocytes, dysregulated compartment-specific cAMP signaling may affect YAP-associated iron homeostasis, LPCAT3-mediated phospholipid remodeling, SLC7A11/GSH/GPX4-dependent antioxidant defenses, and NOX4-related oxidative stress, thereby modifying ferroptosis susceptibility. Together, these pathways provide an integrated mechanistic framework linking neurocardiac signaling imbalance with cardiomyocyte ferroptosis susceptibility. This framework identifies potential targets for preserving adaptive cAMP signaling, improving sympathetic neurotransmitter homeostasis, and limiting ferroptosis-related injury, providing new directions for compartment-specific cardioprotective strategies in heart failure.

title: Optimization and Characterization of a Guinea Pig Model of Diisopropylfluorophosphate-Induced Status Epilepticus, Nitrooxidative Stress, and Neuroinflammation for Therapeutic Evaluation.
abstract: Acute exposure to organophosphate (OP) nerve agents and pesticides induces status epilepticus (SE), nitrooxidative stress, neuroinflammation, and long-term neurological dysfunction. Although rodent models are widely used to study OP-induced neurotoxicity, the guinea pig offers important translational advantages due to its closer similarity to humans in cholinergic physiology and brain organization. The present study aimed to establish and characterize a guinea pig model of diisopropylfluorophosphate (DFP)-induced neurotoxicity suitable for therapeutic evaluation. Unlike the rat model, acute lower doses of DFP (3 or 4mg/kg, s.c.) did not induce behavioral toxicity signs or seizures, while 6mg/kg induced non-convulsive seizures with occasional convulsive seizures. However, 8mg/kg, reliably induced severe and sustained SE (>40min) without mortality. DFP-exposed animals (8mg/kg) transiently lost body weight (~10%) followed by recovery to control levels within three days post-exposure. During the 8 weeks of post-exposure, serum analysis revealed persistent nitro-oxidative stress characterized by elevated nitrite and reactive oxygen species levels, reduced glutathione concentrations, and a decreased GSH/GSSG ratio. DFP exposure (8mg/kg) significantly increased inflammatory cytokines and chemokines in both serum and cerebrospinal fluid, including TNF-α, IL-6, IL-1α, IL-1β, IL-17A, IL-18, and MCP-1 compared to control. Histological analyses revealed increased microgliosis, astrogliosis, and evidence of neurodegeneration in the amygdala, cortex, hippocampus, and thalamus at eight weeks post-DFP exposure (8mg/kg). These findings identify 8mg/kg DFP as the optimal dose for inducing robust status epilepticus (SE), neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, and neurodegeneration without mortality. Collectively, these results support the guinea pig as a clinically relevant higher-order preclinical model for evaluating novel medical countermeasures against organophosphate (OP)-induced neurotoxicity.

title: Influence of Stimulation Parameters on the Analgesic Effect of High-Frequency Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation on Neuropathic Pain: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: There is a need for novel analgesic treatments in patients with chronic neuropathic pain. High-frequency repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (HF-rTMS) may have a clinically significant pain reducing effect. The aim of this study was to evaluate the therapeutic effects of HF-rTMS on chronic neuropathic pain and to investigate the influence of different stimulation parameters. A systematic search in PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science was performed. Thirty-one studies were included. HF-rTMS delivered to the precentral cortex (PreCC) with a focal F8-coil showed a significant analgesic effect (SMD = -0.86, 95% CI [-1.34, -0.37] and SMD = -0.80, 95% CI [-1.39, -0.20], for 3-5-session and >5-session datasets, respectively). HF-rTMS delivered to the PreCC with a larger H-coil also showed a significant effect (SMD = -0.36, 95% CI [-0.65, -0.08]), whereas HF-rTMS delivered to the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex did not (SMD = -0.29, 95% CI [-0.93, 0.34]). Exploratory subgroup analyses did not show statistically significant differences between levels of stimulation frequency, intensity, number of pulses per session, or number of sessions, except for stimulation intensity in the >5-session dataset with the largest effect observed at 80% of the resting motor threshold. Regarding the effects of HF-rTMS of the PreCC, some parameters reached statistical significance at individual level: stimulation frequency (10 Hz in both datasets; 20 Hz in the 3-5-session dataset only), stimulation intensity (80% of the resting motor threshold), and number of pulses per session (1200-1600 in the >5-session dataset; 2000-2500 in the 3-5-session dataset). However, these individual-level significances do not formally establish a difference between subgroups, given that the corresponding comparison tests were not statistically significant. This meta-analysis supports the overall efficacy of HF-rTMS of the PreCC for relieving chronic neuropathic pain. However, given substantial study heterogeneity, statistical limitations, reliance on few or influential studies for several parameter levels, and correlation between parameters across studies, parameter-specific findings should be considered hypothesis-generating rather than evidence of established parameter-response relationships. These results underscore the need for well-powered, systematically designed trials that directly compare stimulation protocols before optimal strategies can be established.

title: Vericiguat attenuates cardiac inflammation and oxidative stress in an obese postmenopausal rat model with concurrent modulation of PKG-I, TGF-β1, and NF-κB.
abstract: Inflammation and oxidative stress are implicated in cardiometabolic changes associated with menopause and obesity. This study investigated the effects of Vericiguat (VER) alone and in combination with estradiol (E2) on oxidative, inflammatory, atherogenic and fibrosis-related markers in cardiac tissue in an ovariectomized rat model of diet-induced obesity. Female Wistar rats were divided into sham and ovariectomized (OVX) groups and fed a standard diet (SD) or high-fat diet (HFD) for 4 months, followed by 4 weeks of treatment with E2, two doses of VER, or their combination. Body weight, malondialdehyde (MDA), total antioxidant capacity (TAC), plasma atherogenic index (AIP), cardiac risk indices I and II (CRI-I and CRI-II), cardiac hydroxyproline, and expression of cardiac PKG-I, NF-κB, and TGF-β1 proteins were assessed. OVX and HFD were associated with increased body weight, AIP, CRI-I, CRI-II, MDA, cardiac NF-κB and TGF-β1 expression, and hydroxyproline content, along with decreased TAC, TAC/MDA ratio, and PKG-I expression. E2 and VER treatments improved these alterations, as evidenced by reductions in AIP, CRI-I, CRI-II, MDA, NF-κB, TGF-β1, and hydroxyproline, as well as increases in TAC, TAC/MDA ratio, and PKG-I expression. Combined treatment with E2 and VER, compared to treatment with E2 alone, significantly improved all these parameters, with the exception of CRI-I and CRI-II. There were significant interactions between E2 and VER treatments were observed for TAC/MDA, hydroxyproline content, and TGF-β1 expression. VER and E2 ameliorated several oxidative, inflammatory, atherogenic, and fibrosis-related changes in this model.

title: Epigenetic Allostasis in Alcohol Use Disorder: A Metabolic-Chromatin Framework Linking DNA Methylation, Circuit Remodeling, and Precision Therapeutics.
abstract: Alcohol Use Disorder (AUD) is a chronic relapsing disorder characterized by persistent dysregulation of reward, stress, and executive circuits. Although acute ethanol effects on neurotransmission are well established, the molecular mechanisms that stabilize long-term vulnerability remain unclear. Building on established allostatic and epigenetic-allostatic models, we develop an expanded framework in which repeated alcohol exposure can drive a transition from adaptive, transient chromatin remodeling toward more persistent epigenetic states across key neural circuits. We integrate evidence from histone modifications, DNA methylation, and metabolic regulation, highlighting how alcohol-induced oxidative stress and disruption of one-carbon metabolism lead to S-adenosylmethionine depletion and methylation instability. These processes converge to form a metabolic-epigenetic trap, reinforcing transcriptional repression of plasticity-related genes. We synthesize circuit-specific changes in the amygdala, prefrontal cortex, nucleus accumbens, and hippocampus, and incorporate emerging human postmortem and single-nucleus multiomic data that support cell-type-specific epigenetic remodeling. In addition, we examine neuroimmune-epigenetic interactions and developmental and sex-dependent exposures as amplifiers of epigenetic vulnerability. Finally, we evaluate therapeutic strategies ranging from selective histone deacetylase inhibition to locus-specific epigenome editing, emphasizing the critical importance of treatment timing and circuit specificity. Together, this expanded framework conceptualizes AUD as a disorder in which maladaptive genomic stability may contribute to persistent circuit dysfunction and identifies epigenetic-metabolic coupling as a testable target for next-generation therapeutics.

title: Oxygen concentration modulates cortical excitability in humans.
abstract: Cortical excitability is fundamental to neuroplasticity, particularly relevant in conditions like stroke and neurodegeneration. Although oxygen is essential for brain metabolism, its effects on cortical excitability remain poorly understood, representing a fundamental gap in neuromodulation research. This study is the first to directly examine the effects of both hypoxia and hyperoxia on corticospinal excitability (CSE) in humans, utilising non-linear analysis of transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) recruitment curves. In a single-blinded, randomised, within-subjects design, 37 participants were exposed to hypoxia (10.5% O2), normoxia (21% O2), and hyperoxia (100% O2). TMS was applied at varying intensities to generate motor-evoked potentials (MEPs), using a Boltzmann Sigmoidal Curve (BSC) approach to optimise estimation of CSE from recruitment curves. Hypoxia enhanced CSE sensitivity at lower intensities, whereas responsiveness was attenuated at higher intensities within the sampled range, potentially due to metabolic constraints. Hyperoxia increased CSE at higher intensities within the sampled range, while saturation could not be accurately estimated with the current sampling. Recruitment curves demonstrated distinct mechanisms, with hypoxia lowering the half-maximal intensity and hyperoxia increasing maximum excitability and slope steepness. These findings show that oxygen levels can modulate CSE in humans, revealing a critical mechanism for enhancing plasticity. Oxygen-based interventions may offer a promising route for improving neurorehabilitation outcomes in clinical populations.

title: XBP-1-mediated suppression of EAAT2 drives glutamate dyshomeostasis and neuronal injury in CORT-induced depression.
abstract: Depression is a prevalent psychiatric disorder characterized by significant social and individual burden. Hippocampal calcium overload and glutamate excitotoxicity are key pathological features, with excitatory amino acid transporter 2 (EAAT2) playing a pivotal role in glutamate clearance. Emerging evidence implicates endoplasmic reticulum stress and its downstream mediator X-box binding protein 1 (XBP-1) in neuronal dysfunction; however, their interaction in depression remains unclear. Here, a corticosterone (CORT)-induced mouse model of depression and a primary hippocampal neuron model were employed to investigate the relationship between XBP-1 and EAAT2. Depressive-like behaviors, neuronal injury, and synaptic and mitochondrial alterations were assessed using behavioral assays, histological and ultrastructural analyses, and functional recordings. CORT exposure was associated with increased hippocampal XBP-1s expression, reduced EAAT2 expression, and elevated glutamate content in hippocampal tissue homogenates. In CORT-treated primary hippocampal neurons, XBP-1 knockdown restored EAAT2 expression and reduced extracellular glutamate accumulation and oxidative stress. In mice, Toyocamycin treatment partially improved depressive-like behaviors and attenuated hippocampal neuronal injury, accompanied by reduced XBP-1s and increased EAAT2 protein levels. These findings support a functional relationship between XBP-1 signaling and EAAT2 expression in the experimental models studied. Whether EAAT2 mediates the protective effects of XBP-1 suppression remains to be established.

title: An in vitro platform for rapid screening of DRG-derived pro-migratory signals in microglia.
abstract: Disturbed crosstalk between somatosensory neurons and immune cells is increasingly recognized as an essential mechanism of pain disorders with a neuroinflammatory component. However, experimental approaches that allow the investigation of factors regulating immune cell migration in the dorsal root ganglion (DRG) remain limited. In this study, we established an in vitro transmigration assay using primary DRG cell cultures and BV2 microglia to assess secretable factors influencing microglia migration. Co-culture with DRG cells significantly increased BV2 cell transmigration, indicating that the DRG culture released pro-migratory signals. As proof of concept, ATP as a well-known component of the DRG secretome markedly stimulated BV2 migration. However, of the broad-spectrum P2 receptor antagonists tested, suramin only partially reduced this effect, whereas pyridoxal phosphate-6-azo (benzene-2,4-disulfonic acid) tetrasodium salt hydrate (PPADS) had no significant inhibitory effect. Surprisingly, neither of the neuropeptides CGRP and substance P nor glutamate were effective at physiological concentrations, indicating that additional releasable factors were involved in regulating the migration response toward DRG cells. Our in vitro platform enables systematic and functional testing of active components of the DRG secretome, providing an accessible tool to dissect neuroimmune communication in health and disease.

title: What Wigglesworth never knew.
Targeting Astrocyte-Neuron Crosstalk in Depression: From Synaptic Mechanisms to Therapeutic Strategies.
journal: Translational research : the journal of laboratory and clinical medicine
abstract: Depression is a leading cause of global disability and imposes a substantial socioeconomic burden worldwide. While traditional theories, such as the monoamine hypothesis and hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis dysfunction, underpin current treatments, existing antidepressants are limited by their delayed onset of action. The tripartite synapse concept contributes to reframing depression, as glia contribute to synaptic dysfunction. Within this framework, astrocytes engage in bidirectional communication with neurons via gliotransmission and modulate synaptic plasticity as integral synaptic components. Postmortem studies have revealed a significant reduction in astrocyte density in the brains of patients with depression, a pathology closely linked to compromised synaptic integrity and loss. In this narrative review, we examine the structural and functional roles of astrocytes in maintaining synaptic homeostasis and explore how astrocytic dysregulation contributes to the pathogenesis of depression. Furthermore, we propose novel therapeutic strategies targeting astrocytes for antidepressant development.

title: Activation of GLP-1 receptors in the middle part of the paraventricular nucleus of thalamus suppresses alcohol-related responses.
abstract: Alcohol use disorder (AUD) remains a major public health challenge, and identifying the brain circuits through which pharmacological interventions act is central to developing more effective treatments. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor (GLP-1R) agonists suppress alcohol-related behaviors in rodents and reduce alcohol consumption in clinical populations with AUD, yet the neuroanatomical substrates mediating these effects remain only partly mapped. One candidate region implicated in addiction is the paraventricular nucleus of the thalamus (PVT), particularly its middle part (mid-PVT), which modulates mesolimbic dopamine signaling, has been implicated in addiction-related processes including alcohol use, and expresses GLP-1R. Whether activation of GLP-1R in the mid-PVT influences alcohol-related responses had not been examined, and that was the aim of the present study. Here, we found that local GLP-1R antagonism in the mid-PVT with exendin-3(9-39) (Ex9) attenuated the suppressive effect of systemically administered GLP-1R agonist exendin-4 (Ex4) on alcohol-induced locomotor stimulation, implicating this region in the central actions of GLP-1R agonists. Intra-mid-PVT Ex4 also attenuated alcohol-induced locomotor stimulation and accumbal dopamine release in male mice, without altering the expression of alcohol-induced conditioned place preference. We further showed that Ex4 into the mid-PVT reduced alcohol intake in male and female rats, although a higher dose was required in females. In a separate cohort of alcohol-consuming, treatment-naive rats, Glp1r mRNA in the PVT did not differ between the sexes. Together, these findings indicate that GLP-1R in the mid-PVT contributes to alcohol-related responses, extending the neuroanatomical map of circuits through which GLP-1R agonists may suppress alcohol intake.

title: Low-level visual and auditory features predict preferences of commercials.
abstract: Video content has become a dominant form of digital marketing, increasing the need to understand which features make videos more appealing and effective. Prior studies showed that low-level visual features in static images affect saliency and consumer preferences, while low-level auditory features influence preferences for music clips. However, it remains unclear how these features and their interaction shape preferences for dynamic stimuli such as video commercials. In this study, 165 participants watched 100 video commercials and rated how much they liked each commercial and their willingness to pay (WTP) for the advertised product. We extracted low-level visual and auditory features from the commercials (e.g., colorfulness, scene frequency, zero-crossing rate) and used them as inputs to linear and non-linear prediction models. Both visual and auditory low-level features significantly predicted Liking and WTP, with the combined model performing best. Importantly, these low-level features also predicted the aggregate engagement metrics at the population level as measured on YouTube, demonstrating the generalizability of our findings and their external validity. These findings show that low-level sensory information influences consumer preferences and ad effectiveness and demonstrate how computational tools can be used to evaluate video effectiveness.

title: A systematic review and meta-analysis of quantitative pain outcomes in degenerative thoracic myelopathy.
abstract: Degenerative thoracic myelopathy (DTM) refers to symptomatic compression of the thoracic spinal cord secondary to degenerative pathology, including thoracic disc herniation (TDH), ossification of the ligamentum flavum (OLF) and ossification of the posterior longitudinal ligament (OPLL). Sensorimotor impairments and sphincter dysfunction often accompany pain, yet quantitative characterisation of pain and pain-related functional disability outcomes remains limited. We aimed to synthesise quantitative pain outcomes in DTM. The review was registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261297878) and conducted following PRISMA guidelines. MEDLINE and Embase were searched from inception until December 2025. Screening and data extraction were performed in duplicate and all risk-of-bias scoring was cross-checked. Findings were synthesised by random-effects meta-analyses for cohorts with sufficient data to estimate the standard deviation of change in pain. Cohorts not included in the meta-analysis were synthesised following the SWiM guidelines. Twenty-eight studies comprising 1,225 patients within 34 cohorts met inclusion criteria. Every cohort improved after surgery (34/34 for the visual analogue scale (VAS); 10/10 for the Oswestry Disability Index (ODI)). In the 19 VAS cohorts that could be weighted (578 patients), the pooled reduction was 3.45 cm (95% CI 2.88-4.03; I2 = 94.5%), and in the nine ODI cohorts that could be weighted (145 patients) the pooled reduction was 29.4 points (20.9-37.8; I2 = 97.3%). The pooled VAS reduction was 4.06 cm in TDH and 3.34 cm in OLF cohorts. The 10 VAS cohorts that could not be weighted (436 patients) were synthesised descriptively, with a median of the reported mean reductions of 4.28 cm (IQR 3.85-4.63). Similar reductions were reported for discectomy with and without fusion. Only six studies reported axial pain separately from non-axial pain; consistent differentiation of pain subtypes and standardised reporting of pain measures are needed to strengthen the evidence base. Surgery for DTM appears to be associated with reductions in pain and pain-related functional disability, although substantial heterogeneity and the uncontrolled design of studies mean that certainty of the evidence is currently very low. PROSPERO, CRD420261297878.

title: Developmental disruption of the mediodorsal thalamus alters prefrontal dopamine D2 receptor expression and prefrontal-accumbal neuronal recruitment during latent inhibition.
abstract: The mediodorsal thalamus (MD) is a higher-order thalamic nucleus that plays a central role in the maturation and function of prefrontal cortical circuits. Although developmental MD dysfunction has been implicated in cognitive deficits associated with neurodevelopmental disorders, the underlying molecular and circuit mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated whether neonatal MD lesions produce persistent alterations in latent inhibition (LI), prefrontal dopamine D2 receptor (D2R) expression, and neuronal recruitment within the MD-prefrontal cortex (PFC)-nucleus accumbens (NAc) circuit. Bilateral excitotoxic MD lesions were induced in Sprague-Dawley rats on postnatal day 4 (MD lesion n = 35; MD Sham n = 35). In adulthood, LI was assessed using a conditioned taste aversion paradigm. Neuronal activation was evaluated by c-Fos immunohistochemistry, whereas D2R expression was quantified by immunohistochemistry, Western blotting, and quantitative PCR. The ability of the D2R antagonist haloperidol to restore LI and neuronal activity was also examined. Neonatal MD lesions produced a persistent impairment of LI accompanied by reduced task-related c-Fos expression in the PFC and NAc. These functional abnormalities were associated with a selective increase in prefrontal D2R expression at the transcript, protein, and cellular levels, whereas no changes were observed in the secondary motor cortex. Importantly, haloperidol administration during stimulus pre-exposure restored LI and normalized c-Fos activation in the PFC and NAc of MD-lesion animals without affecting sham controls. These findings demonstrate that early MD dysfunction induces long-lasting remodeling of prefrontal dopaminergic signaling and disrupts recruitment of the MD-PFC-NAc circuit during selective attention. They identify altered D2R signaling as a potential mechanism linking developmental thalamic dysfunction to persistent cognitive deficits.

title: Sex-specific personality metatrait profiles and their associations with APOE, PICALM variants, and cognitive performance in healthy middle-aged adults: a cluster-based analysis.
abstract: APOE ε4 is the strongest common genetic risk factor for late-onset Alzheimer's disease, while PICALM rs3851179 has been associated with amyloid-β clearance. Personality can be summarized into two higher-order metatraits: Stability, reflecting emotional and behavioral regulation, and Plasticity, reflecting cognitive flexibility. This study examined whether genetic associations with episodic memory and fluid intelligence differ across Stability-Plasticity personality clusters in cognitively healthy middle-aged adults. The sample comprised 192 participants. NEO-FFI personality traits were standardized to derive the metatraits Stability and Plasticity. Sex-stratified agglomerative hierarchical clustering (Ward's linkage) identified two personality profiles characterized by relatively higher or lower levels of both metatraits. Cognitive outcomes included the California Verbal Learning Test (CVLT) and Raven's Progressive Matrices (RPM). Sex-stratified regression models examined associations between APOE ε4 carrier status, PICALM rs3851179 GG genotype, age, education, and cognitive performance. After false discovery rate correction, significant associations were observed only in females. In the low Stability-low Plasticity cluster, the APOE × age interaction was negatively associated with CVLT Recognition performance (pFDR = 0.019; R2 = 0.254). In the high Stability-high Plasticity cluster, models incorporating APOE and/or PICALM status were significantly associated with CVLT Recognition performance (R2 = 0.583-0.619, pFDR = 0.010-0.019). For fluid intelligence, significant negative APOE × age and APOE × age × education interactions, as well as a negative APOE × PICALM × age interaction, were observed in the respective models (R2 = 0.553-0.696, pFDR = 0.001-0.019). Personality metatraits were associated with variability in APOE-related cognitive outcomes, particularly among females. These findings suggest that personality structure can contribute to individual differences in cognitive aging pathways associated with genetic risk. However, the results should be interpreted considering the cross-sectional design and limited sample size.

title: Recent advances in the pharmacological effects and mechanisms of borneol and borneol-containing formulations in central nervous system diseases.
abstract: Borneol is an aromatic medicinal agent widely used in traditional Chinese medicine, both as a standalone component and as an ingredient in multi-herb formulations. Its pharmacological relevance to central nervous system (CNS) disorders has attracted increasing attention, particularly in Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, epilepsy, ischemic stroke, and glioma. Accumulating evidence indicates that borneol may influence multiple pathophysiological processes, including brain-barrier function and drug delivery, neuroinflammation and oxidative stress, neurotransmitter homeostasis and neuronal excitability, cellular injury and death, and the clearance of pathological substances and post-injury repair. Here, we integrate and compare these mechanisms across disease contexts. Notably, although several actions of borneol appear to converge across CNS disorders, others are strongly disease- and context-dependent; for example, its effects on brain-barrier permeability, oxidative stress, and cell death may differ in direction according to disease pathology and therapeutic intent. Pharmacokinetic studies support measurable brain exposure to borneol, yet direct comparative evidence of pharmacological activity, brain disposition, and human pharmacokinetics among borneol preparations of different botanical origins and stereochemical configurations remains scarce. Borneol-containing formulations also exhibit multi-level pharmacological effects; however, because most studies lack borneol-alone, borneol-depleted, or add-back controls, these effects cannot be unequivocally attributed to borneol itself. Overall, the current evidence base remains dominated by cellular and animal studies, with several proposed mechanisms inferred primarily from changes in molecular expression or computational predictions. Robust causal validation, high-quality clinical evidence, and long-term safety data are still limited. Future studies should therefore define the dose-exposure-response relationships and disease-specific therapeutic windows of different borneol preparations, establish the independent contribution of borneol within complex formulations, and determine its genuine therapeutic value and long-term safety through rigorous mechanistic and clinical investigation.

title: Transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation in perioperative neurocognitive disorders: clinical evidence and mechanistic perspectives.
