abstract: Perioperative neurocognitive disorders (PND) are common neurological complications in older surgical patients and are associated with impaired recovery, loss of independence, and worse quality of life. Transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) is a non-invasive neuromodulatory intervention with plausible effects on inflammatory, autonomic, sleep, pain, and cognitive-network pathways. We conducted a PROSPERO-registered systematic review of direct perioperative randomized clinical evidence and, when outcomes were sufficiently comparable, an exploratory meta-analysis. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science Core Collection, and CENTRAL were searched from inception through 5 August 2026. Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 and certainty with GRADE. Mechanistic and translational evidence was synthesized separately using a structured narrative approach. Four randomized trials enrolled or randomized 480 participants, of whom 469 contributed to reported analyses. Two trials involving 220 participants assessed related but non-identical early postoperative cognitive-decline constructs: one used dNCR and the other investigator-defined traditional POCD. Both studies individually favored taVNS, and the individual study estimates were treated as the primary evidence. A post hoc exploratory cross-construct synthesis yielded an RR of 0.34 (95% CI 0.18-0.64). Because the contributing trials used non-equivalent cognitive definitions, stimulation regimens, and comparator conditions, this secondary pooled estimate should not be interpreted as representing either a single standardized cognitive outcome or the effect of a single standardized taVNS intervention. A separate multicenter trial reported postoperative delirium in 12.0% versus 25.3% of participants (risk ratio 0.47, 95% confidence interval 0.23-0.98), and another trial showed more favorable postoperative Montreal Cognitive Assessment trajectories. Beyond clinical outcomes, the broader mechanistic literature supports a multilevel neurophysiological rationale for taVNS, consistent with possible modulation of auricular vagal afferent-nucleus tractus solitarius signaling, locus coeruleus and autonomic regulation, inflammatory reflex pathways, splenic sympathetic-cholinergic immune modulation, blood-brain barrier/neurovascular unit protection, glial responses, sleep-arousal regulation, and cognitive-network plasticity. However, most mechanistic evidence remains derived from preclinical or non-perioperative studies, and no causal pathway linking target engagement to cognitive improvement has been established. Current evidence suggests a promising but preliminary clinical signal for taVNS in perioperative neurocognitive disorders. However, certainty remains low to very low, and routine clinical implementation is not yet supported. Available adverse-event data are insufficient to establish perioperative safety or to exclude uncommon cardiovascular or autonomic adverse events. Standardized PND outcomes, credible sham conditions, optimized stimulation dose and timing, systematic adverse-event ascertainment, multimodal target-engagement biomarkers, and risk-enriched confirmatory trials are priorities for future development. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261468039, Identifier: CRD420261468039.

title: Establishing a novel sepsis-associated brain dysfunction model in zebrafish larvae.
abstract: As a common complication of sepsis, sepsis-associated encephalopathy (SAE) was observed with high mortality, but there were less effective therapeutic strategies due to disease complexity. This study aimed to establish and characterize a larval zebrafish model of sepsis-associated brain dysfunction (SBD) suitable for phenotypic assessment and compound screening. The SBD zebrafish larvae model was established by lipopolysaccharide (LPS) injection into the peritoneal cavity. Sepsis-induced inflammation of the intestine and brain was assessed using transgenic fluorescent larvae. The infection's influence on intestine structure and brain function was monitored by HE staining, fluorescence staining, and behavioral assessment. Simultaneously, 16S rRNA sequencing and whole-larva transcriptomic profiling were conducted to characterize larva-associated microbial changes and systemic molecular responses. The expression of genes involved in inflammation, barrier function, ferroptosis as well as apoptosis was quantified via qPCR. After LPS treatment for 24 h, there were significant neutrophil infiltration, increasing peristalsis, structural damage, and upregulated inflammatory gene expression in the intestine. Traced by using 10 kDa dextran-tetramethylrhodamine, the zebrafish larvae were observed with obviously increased fluorescence in the brain. In combination with downregulated tight junction genes, it suggested the breakdown of blood-brain barrier permeability. Simultaneously, we found increasing apoptotic cells, infiltrated neutrophils as well as imbalanced neurotransmitters in the larvae brain, and they exhibited reduced locomotor activity and altered color-preference/exploratory behavior. The 16S rRNA sequencing and transcriptome results showed restructuring of the larva-associated microbial community, including an increased relative abundance of Aeromonas. Whole-larva transcriptomic profiling identified a prominent ferroptosis-related signature, which was supported by increased ROS levels, altered ferroptosis-related gene expression, and mitochondrial changes. Increased lipid peroxidation provided additional support for ferroptosis-related alterations. We successfully developed a novel sepsis-associated brain dysfunction zebrafish larvae model. Based on its advantages of high throughput, rapidity, visualization, and facile gene edition, this model is expected to be beneficial for SAE drug discovery and disease mechanism exploration.

title: Resolving the apparent paradox of multisensory expertise: coupling priors, common-cause priors, and how to distinguish among them.
abstract: Perceptual expertise is widely assumed to refine multisensory perception, yet the empirical literature appears inconsistent. Trained musicians show narrower audiovisual temporal integration windows and quicker segregation, whereas experienced wine tasters seem more influenced by a wine's color in their aroma and flavor judgments than novices are. We argue that the inconsistency arises from a conflation of two formally distinct quantities: the prior probability that concurrent signals arise from a common source, and the coupling between the values of signals that share one. We present a generative model in which both are free parameters, along with channel precision and a decision criterion, that contains causal-inference and coupling-prior models as special cases. The model shows that the correlation between the values of two signals across an environment reflects only the product of the two priors, so that a correlation-tracking learner acquires the coupling when the signals always share a source, whereas separating the two priors requires representing causal structure; that binary common-source reports confound the common-cause prior with the decision criterion; that the coupling trades off against the measurement noise of the influencing channel unless its precision is measured independently; and that the two priors leave distinct signatures in how cross-modal influence varies with disparity. When the source is fixed, as for the color and odor of a wine, tighter coupling alone produces the conjunction of greater displacement by color and better discrimination between wines reported for experienced tasters, which no change in odor precision can produce. Simulations of a test battery combining continuous estimates, common-source reports and discrimination thresholds show that the parameters can be recovered, that a within-subject dissociation can be detected with conventional sample sizes under illustrative effect sizes, and that recovery fails in certain cases. The account yields a rule classifying environments by their base rate of common causation and their coupling strength, and the same ambiguity attends claims about altered multisensory processing in autism and aging. We also show that the most cited demonstration of expert susceptibility to color contains no expertise manipulation, and suggest that apparent expert biases may reflectwind calibration to real-world statistics.

title: Editorial: Emerging talents in human neuroscience: psychophysiology and cognitive neuroscience 2025.
Thalamic remodeling underlying below-level neuropathic pain following spinal cord injury: neuroimmune, neurochemical, and circuit-level mechanisms.
abstract: Below-level neuropathic pain (BLNP) is a common and refractory complication of spinal cord injury (SCI). Its persistence and significant clinical heterogeneity are difficult to explain solely through mechanisms within the injured spinal cord. The thalamus receives ascending sensory input from the spinal cord and has extensive connections with the somatosensory cortex, insula, and cingulate cortex; sustained thalamic remodeling may serve as a critical mechanism by which abnormal spinal activity drives central pain processing. Existing evidence indicates that partial sensory deafferentation and abnormal neural activity transmitted via spared pathways can alter thalamic afferent input, while signaling involving C-C motif chemokine ligand 21 (CCL21) may influence the local neuroimmune environment of the thalamus. Microglial responses, altered excitatory-inhibitory synaptic regulation, changes in ion-channel expression, and synaptic structural modifications are all associated with hyperexcitability and aberrant firing patterns in thalamic neurons. These local changes may also be accompanied by the reorganization of corticothalamic feedback and alterations in thalamocortical functional connectivity. Human imaging studies suggest that pain phenotypes are associated with thalamic metabolism, related white-matter microstructure, and functional connectivity. This review examines thalamic afferent status, neuroimmune signaling, neurochemical and electrophysiological changes, and the reorganization of related circuits to enhance understanding of supraspinal mechanisms, systematically consolidate existing evidence, and provide a basis for investigating thalamus-related candidate clinical measures and mechanism-based interventions.

title: Under-recognized Autoimmune Encephalitis in Patients with Alzheimer's Disease: A Case Series Emphasizing EEG Screening.
abstract: AD and AE present overlapping cognitive decline, often causing misdiagnosis and delayed immunotherapy. AD has an insidious onset and slow progression with typical Aβ and tau abnormalities, while AE manifests subacute neuropsychiatric symptoms and inflammatory imaging or CSF changes. Rapid cognitive decline in AD patients with superimposed AE is easily misdiagnosed as simple neurodegeneration. EEG is a convenient non-invasive test that can serve as a screening tool to trigger further autoimmune evaluation in AD patients with unexplained rapid deterioration. This case series reports two verified AD patients complicated with anti-LGI1 encephalitis and probable seronegative AE. It adds to the literature on the pathological coexistence and interaction of AD and AE, highlights the underutilized diagnostic value of EEG, and supports routine EEG screening for rapidly progressive AD cognitive decline. Two biomarker-confirmed AD female patients with comorbid AE were included. The 75-year-old patient had 4 years of cognitive decline (baseline MMSE=10), with typical AD imaging and biomarker abnormalities, positive anti-LGI1 IgG and abnormal EEG, diagnosed with AD combined with LGI1 encephalitis. She received IVIg, rituximab, anti-amyloid and anti-dementia treatment. MMSE improved from 10 to 18 at 1 month but fluctuated thereafter (MMSE 11-12, MoCA 3-9) with treatment pause and irregular adherence; serum LGI1 antibody and AD biomarkers remained normal throughout. The 62-year-old patient had 7 years of cognitive decline, personality changes, and hallucinations (MMSE=0, MoCA=0). She was diagnosed with probable seronegative AE complicated with AD based on AD imaging changes, positive CSF indicators, and positive TBA findings. Treatment with telitacicept and lecanemab was associated with modest cognitive improvement (MMSE +3, MoCA +2) at short-term follow-up. Rapid cognitive exacerbation in AD patients should not be attributed to natural neurodegeneration. Routine EEG is an essential noninvasive tool for cognitive evaluation in AD. EEG abnormalities in AD patients require comprehensive autoimmune examinations. Concurrent AE is a reversible and treatable factor worsening AD cognitive impairment. Combined immunotherapy and anti-amyloid treatment can significantly improve patient cognition and biomarkers. EEG should be a routine screening item for rapidly progressive AD. Autoimmune inflammation may accelerate AD progression, providing new insights for AD immunological pathogenesis and targeted therapy research.

title: OsGST Positively Regulates Root Cell Wall Phosphorus Reutilization in P-Deficient Rice Through an NO-Associated Pathway.
abstract: Limited phosphorus (P) availability strongly restricts rice growth and yield formation. Glutathione S-transferases (GSTs) participate in stress responses, but their roles in rice adaptation to low P remain unclear. Here, we characterized a Tau-class GST gene, OsGST (LOC_Os10g38160/OsGSTU22), in rice under P deficiency. Loss-of-function osgst mutants showed weaker growth and lower soluble, total, and xylem P levels under -P, whereas OsGST-overexpressing lines showed improved growth and higher P accumulation. OsGST was preferentially expressed in roots and induced by P deficiency. Under P deficiency, the osgst mutants retained more P in root cell wall and pectin fractions than Nip, accompanied by higher pectin methylesterification, lower NO accumulation, reduced Oryza sativa phosphate transporter 2/6/8 (OsPT2/6/8) transcript levels, disrupted glutathione homeostasis, and increased ROS accumulation. Application of the NO donor sodium nitroprusside reduced the differences in cell wall P mobilization and P accumulation between Nipponbare and osgst mutants. These results suggest that OsGST promotes rice adaptation to P deficiency by maintaining redox homeostasis and facilitating NO-associated root cell wall P reutilization.

title: Risk factors for seizures in patients with brain metastases: integrating clinical features and molecular markers.
abstract: Brain metastases (BM) affect nearly 30% of patients with solid tumors. Despite this prevalence, the mechanisms underlying brain tumor-related epilepsy (BTRE) in this population remain incompletely elucidated. This study aims to investigate risk factors associated with seizure occurrence in patients with BM, focusing on histology and molecular markers of the primary tumor. We conducted a retrospective cohort study on 325 patients who underwent surgical resection of BM between 2014 and 2019. Clinical, radiological, and molecular data were analyzed using univariate and multivariable regression models to assess seizure risk factors. Overall Survival (OS) was assessed using Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression models. Seizures occurred in 32% of patients. Frontal (P<0.001) and parietal (P=0.05) locations were significantly associated with seizure occurrence. Ovarian cancer exhibited the highest seizure prevalence (80%, P=0.001), followed by melanoma (44%), breast (35%), and colorectal cancer (34%). Regarding molecular status, we found a significant association between seizures and both BRAF mutations in melanoma (P=0.03) and HER2 positive subtype breast cancer (P=0.01). Seizure occurrence at onset correlated with improved OS (P=0.01). Our findings suggest an association between seizure risk and molecular status of the primary tumor, specifically BRAF mutations in melanoma and HER2+ breast cancer subtype. Additionally, we found an improved OS in BM patients experiencing seizures at onset of disease. These findings are exploratory and warrant confirmation in larger cohorts; this could help refine seizure-risk estimation and prognostic assessment in surgically treated patients with brain metastases.

title: Stem cell therapy attenuates cerebellar histological alterations and blood-brain barrier disruption in experimental fibromyalgia: involvement of mast cells, autophagy, and NLRP3/IL-1β neuroinflammatory pathway.
abstract: Fibromyalgia is a prevalent and debilitating condition that results in generalized musculoskeletal pain, trouble sleeping, exhaustion, psychological challenges, and social problems. As a consequence of fibromyalgia's substantial therapeutic and socioeconomic burden caused by its high prevalence, uncertain etiology, wide spectrum of clinical manifestations, and sophisticated therapy, a considerable interest has emerged in investigating novel aspects of its pathophysiology, particularly those related to anxiety, depression, and cerebellar histological alterations. Such investigations may contribute to the development of effective therapeutic strategies, including the use of bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) as a promising treatment approach. Rats were randomly divided into three groups: control, fibromyalgia and fibromyalgia-stem cell groups. Behavioral assessment was carried out. Cerebellar cortices were collected for histological, immunohistochemical, and morphometric analysis. Fibromyalgia group revealed anxiety-like behavioral changes, and neurodegenerative changes with blood-brain barrier (BBB) affection. Furthermore, NLRP3 and IL-1β immune-expression were significantly increased, with significant increase in the total number of mast cells with marked degranulation. Additionally, there was a significant decrease in Calbindin D-28k (CB), Beclin-1 and LC3 immune-expression. Fibromyalgia-stem cells group revealed amelioration in behavioral alterations, histological improvement, significant decrease in CD117, NLRP3 and IL-1β immune-expression, besides a significant increase in CB, Beclin-1 and LC3 immune-expression. This study represents one of the first experimental studies investigating the potential therapeutic value of BMSCs therapy in fibromyalgia-related cerebellar damage through neuroprotective mechanisms involving enhancement of autophagy, mast cell deactivation, and suppression of NLRP3/IL-1β mediated neuroinflammation with improvement of BBB structural integrity.

title: Longitudinal evolution of O-(2-[18F]-fluoroethyl)-L-tyrosine PET metrics in serial imaging during glioblastoma progression.
abstract: Most studies evaluating O-(2-[18F]-fluoroethyl)-L-tyrosine (FET) PET for glioblastoma progression rely on single-scan assessments, leaving diagnostic uncertainties in cases with borderline tracer uptake. We evaluated metabolic activity evolution during the transition of glioblastoma progression using serial FET PET to determine whether longitudinal parameter changes improve diagnostic certainty. Between 2016 and 2026, 182 patients with glioblastoma undergoing 690 dynamic FET PET scans (median, 3; range, 2-12) were retrospectively evaluated. Eligible cases required documented progressive disease according to RANO 2.0 criteria and serial FET PET at least 2 time points (at suspected progression and within a 6-month prior window). Static PET parameters, ie tumor-to-brain ratios (TBRmean, TBRmax) and metabolic tumor volume (MTV), and their longitudinal changes were evaluated according to PET RANO 1.0 criteria, alongside additional dynamic PET parameters (time-to-peak). Single-scan metrics and serial changes were compared in cases with borderline uptake. Ninety patients with 102 confirmed progression events met all selection criteria (median interscan interval, 2.7 months). At progression, TBRmean, TBRmax, and MTV increased significantly (P < .001). Median percentage increases were modest for TBRmean (+4%) and TBRmax (+17%), whereas MTV exhibited a substantial expansion (+182%). In cases with borderline uptake, applying a longitudinal MTV increase criterion of ≥40% per PET RANO 1.0 substantially improved progression detection to up to 89%, yielding a 14% higher diagnostic detection rate compared to single-scan thresholds. In glioblastomas with documented RANO 2.0 progression, integrating longitudinal MTV changes markedly improves diagnostic certainty over single-scan uptake metrics, particularly in challenging cases with borderline uptake.

title: Defining and managing NF1-related peripheral nerve sheath tumors at risk for malignant transformation: Consensus from the Atypical Neurofibroma Symposium.
abstract: People with neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) are at risk for developing peripheral nerve sheath tumors (PNSTs) ranging from benign neurofibromas to high-grade sarcomas. PNSTs known as atypical neurofibromas are at increased risk for malignant transformation. In 2017 the term ANNUBP (atypical neurofibromatous neoplasm of uncertain biologic potential) was proposed for PNSTs at increased risk for malignant transformation based on histopathologic features. Subsequently it was recognized that PNSTs not meeting ANNUBP criteria could still have concerning clinical, imaging and molecular features. A State of the Science conference addressed how to define these pre-cancerous PNSTs and reached consensus regarding clinical management and priority areas of research. Key recommendations from this symposium include: (1) using a combination of histologic, molecular and imaging features to define pre-malignant "at-risk" PNST; (2) recognizing that people with NF1 may be divided into "higher-risk" and "average-risk" for MPNST based on features such as their germline NF1 variant, internal tumor burden and history of malignancy or radiotherapy and; (3) the need to validate consensus screening and surveillance strategies based on personal and tumor-related risk factors. These recommendations will advance the ability to standardize care, and potentially fuel research that enables early diagnosis, prevention of malignant transformation and improved outcomes.

title: Combined MEG and EEG suggest a limbic source network for the P3.
abstract: The event-related P3 is evoked by most task-relevant or salient stimuli, but its neural sources remain controversial. Here we reevaluate the role of hippocampus, unambiguously demonstrated in intracranial recordings, and retro-splenial cortex as sources of the P3 in magneto- and electroencephalography. Observers detected rare visual targets of a deviant shape and ignored rare non-targets of a deviant color. Source analysis was based on noise-normalized minimum-norm estimates in an individual, MRI-based source space. Critically, the cortical source space was extended to include the cornu ammonis of the hippocampus. Source analysis at the P3 peak showed strong sources in retrosplenial cortex and a weaker source in hippocampus. Activity in left somatosensory cortex was related to the button presses. Subsequent activity was observed in insula and anterior mid-cingulate cortex. Further simulation studies explored the spread of these sources and the plausibility of their combination to explain the data, and demonstrate that the combination of magneto- and electroencephalography increased the specificity of the source estimate. Overall, these data support an interpretation of the P3 as physiological indicator of activity in the limbic system for target and distractor stimuli.

title: FLT3 Kinase Inhibition Reshapes the Neuronal Transcriptome to Suppress Seizures.
journal: Molecular therapy : the journal of the American Society of Gene Therapy
abstract: Approximately one-third of individuals with epilepsy are refractory to current anti-seizure medications, highlighting the need for new, mechanism-based therapeutic approaches. Fms-like tyrosine kinase 3 (FLT3), a receptor tyrosine kinase classically studied in hematopoiesis and leukemia, is also expressed in neurons, although its function in the brain remains largely unexplored. Our prior work identified small-molecule FLT3 inhibitors (FLT3i) as unexpected enhancers of potassium-chloride cotransporter 2 (KCC2), a neuron-specific chloride transporter essential for maintaining GABAergic inhibition. Here, we applied a functional genomics framework in mouse primary neurons and human stem cell-derived neurons to define FLT3i-induced transcriptional programs, revealing conserved gene networks governing synaptic function and ion channel regulation. A complementary CRISPR/Cas9-based screen of candidate transcription factors identified FLT3-responsive neuronal gene regulatory networks linked to epigenetic remodeling and neuroinflammatory signaling. We further demonstrate that KW-2449, an orally bioavailable FLT3 inhibitor, penetrates the blood-brain barrier, elevates KCC2 expression in vivo for up to 24 hours, and significantly reduces seizure susceptibility in a kainic acid-induced mouse model of epilepsy. Together, these findings reveal a previously unrecognized role for FLT3 in neuronal function and establish proof-of-principle for FLT3 inhibition as a mechanistically supported candidate strategy warranting further development as a next-generation anti-seizure therapy.

title: Periodontitis as a Modifiable Risk Factor for Dementia: Mechanistic Pathways Linking Oral Inflammation to Neurodegeneration.
journal: The Canadian journal of neurological sciences. Le journal canadien des sciences neurologiques
abstract: Emerging evidence increasingly implicates chronic periodontal disease as a contributor to age-related cognitive decline and dementia, including Alzheimer's disease (AD). Periodontitis is defined by persistent oral microbial dysbiosis, ulcerated gingival epithelium, repeated bacteremia and sustained systemic inflammatory signaling - factors that plausibly influence neuroimmune pathways and cerebrovascular integrity. This review synthesizes findings from epidemiological studies, systematic reviews, mechanistic analyses and experimental models to examine the biological links between oral inflammation and neurodegeneration. Collectively, the literature suggests a stepwise oral-brain axis: first gingival inflammation promotes local and systemic pro-inflammatory cytokine release, second repeated bacteremia allows oral pathogens and microbial byproducts to enter circulation, third these signals and agents access and compromise the blood-brain barrier, then fourth microglia in the brain become primed and hyper-reactive and at last enhanced neuroinflammation accelerates amyloid-β and tau pathology. Although causal inference remains limited by the predominance of observational data, emerging intervention studies and mechanistic evidence suggest that periodontal health is a potentially modifiable factor in dementia prevention strategies.

title: Comparison of DHEA- and Letrozole-Induced Polycystic Ovary Syndrome Phenotypes in Rats Under Simulated High-Altitude Hypoxia.
journal: Medical science monitor : international medical journal of experimental and clinical research
abstract: BACKGROUND Exposure to high altitudes and low oxygen levels has been associated with female reproductive system damage and increased polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) incidence. This study compared the effects of dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA) injection and letrozole gavage on development of PCOS-like phenotypes in rats under simulated high-altitude hypoxic (HH) conditions. MATERIAL AND METHODS Eighty late-adolescent Sprague-Dawley rats received subcutaneous DHEA injections or letrozole gavage under simulated HH conditions at 6000 m (pressure: 47.2 kPa) or local ambient altitude (LA; 2200 m; pressure: 77.2 kPa) for 21 days. Body weight, serum reproductive hormone levels, ovarian histomorphology, and estrous cycles were evaluated. RESULTS Under HH conditions, DHEA-treated rats had higher body weights than letrozole-treated rats (mean difference=-8.367, P=0.040). DHEA injection increased testosterone levels (adjusted P<0.001), while decreasing estradiol (adjusted P<0.001) and progesterone levels (adjusted P<0.001). Letrozole gavage increased only testosterone levels (adjusted P=0.008); there were no significant changes in estradiol or progesterone levels. The DHEA group exhibited more severe follicular atresia and a greater reduction in the healthy-to-cystic follicle ratio than the letrozole group (adjusted P=0.046). DHEA injection also produced more complete estrous cycle disruption than letrozole gavage under both LA and HH conditions by day 21 (100% vs 30% under LA and 100% vs 60% under HH; P=0.003 and P=0.011, respectively). CONCLUSIONS Under simulated HH conditions, DHEA injection produces a more severe PCOS-like reproductive phenotype than letrozole gavage. Further studies are needed to expand these findings across altitudes, exposure durations, and age groups.

title: EXPRESS: Blood-free full quantification of dynamic TSPO PET imaging with [11C]PBR28.
journal: Journal of cerebral blood flow and metabolism : official journal of the International Society of Cerebral Blood Flow and Metabolism
abstract: Quantitative dynamic PET imaging requires metabolite-corrected arterial input functions, traditionally obtained through invasive arterial blood sampling, limiting broader adoption of quantitative kinetic modelling. Achieving generalisability across datasets, scanners, and imaging centres remains a major challenge for data-driven alternatives. We developed ASTRA, a deep-learning-based framework for arterial input function estimation from dynamic brain TSPO PET. ASTRA was developed and validated using arterial measurements in one dataset (n=90), then transfer-learned and evaluated against arterial measurements at a second centre (n=52). Building upon this, ASTRA was applied to an independent clinical cohort (n=32) from the second site but without arterial reference data, where quantitative analyses had therefore not been performed, to assess whether it could reproduce previously reported semi-quantitative cross-sectional group differences. Robustness to altered tracer kinetics was evaluated in an out-of-distribution pharmacological blockade cohort (n=5). ASTRA-derived quantitative estimates agreed with arterial measurements (VT: CCC=0.658-0.805), with higher uncertainty associated with greater error. In the clinical cohort, ASTRA reproduced SUVR-based group differences using DVR (p<0.001), except in the pituitary gland (p=0.12). Finally, ASTRA yielded receptor occupancy estimates (0.92±0.17) closely matching arterial values (0.94±0.12) in the blocking cohort. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of multi-site, non-invasive quantitative TSPO PET.

title: Reactive Oxygen Species Modulator 1 Promotes Tumor Progression and Angiogenesis via the ROS-HIF-1α Axis in Lung Adenocarcinoma.
abstract: Reactive oxygen species modulator 1 (Romo1) regulates intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) production. It has been reported to be upregulated in various cancers and contributes to tumor growth and metastasis. However, the role of Romo1 in tumor angiogenesis remains unclear. Bioinformatic analysis assessed Romo1 expression and clinical significance in LUAD. Romo1 overexpression and knockdown were used to examine ROS production and expression of hypoxia-inducible factor-1α (HIF-1α) and vascular endothelial growth factor A (VEGFA). YC-1, a HIF-1α inhibitor, was used to determine whether these effects are mediated by Romo1-induced HIF-1α upregulation. Pathway enrichment analysis and HIF-1α signature scoring were performed. Romo1 is highly expressed in LUAD and is associated with aggressive pathological features and a poor prognosis. Romo1 induced ROS production and increased the expression of HIF-1α and VEGFA. Pathway enrichment analysis linked Romo1-associated oxidative stress to the HIF-1 signaling pathway and angiogenesis. Romo1 enhanced the angiogenic activity of endothelial cells and tumor cell proliferation. In a mouse xenograft tumor model, Romo1 promoted tumor growth and angiogenesis through HIF-1α upregulation. HIF-1α inhibition suppressed Romo1-induced tumor cell proliferation and the angiogenic activities. Analysis of the LUAD dataset revealed a positive association between ROMO1 mRNA expression and HIF-1α signaling pathway activation. These findings provide novel insights into the mechanisms by which Romo1 contributes to tumor progression and angiogenesis in LUAD.

title: The 2026 Taiwan headache society guideline on the use of treatments targeting the CGRP pathway.
journal: Journal of the Chinese Medical Association : JCMA
abstract: The introduction of CGRP-targeted therapy has markedly influenced migraine care in Taiwan, together with accumulating evidence and clinical experience. Therefore, the Treatment Guideline Subcommittee of the Taiwan Headache Society updated its 2022 consensus on preventive migraine therapy, with a specific focus on CGRP-targeted therapies. This updated guideline also provides evidence-based recommendations and practical guidance on the use of gepants following their introduction in Taiwan. After reviewing recent clinical trials, meta-analyses, and international guidelines, and integrating expert panel opinions, we developed this new guideline to update the treatment options, recommended populations, timing of initiation and discontinuation, and practical considerations for CGRP-targeted therapy, organised into ten clinical questions. According to the current consensus, preventive treatment is recommended for patients with ≥4 headache days per month, significant disability, failure of or contraindications to acute therapy, complicated migraine with severe aura (such as hemiplegic migraine or migrainous infarction), or when patient preference favours prevention after balancing potential benefits and risks. Currently, CGRP-targeted therapies for migraine prevention include anti-CGRP monoclonal antibodies, namely erenumab, fremanezumab, galcanezumab, and eptinezumab, as well as small-molecule CGRP receptor antagonists, including rimegepant and atogepant. In this 2026 updated guideline, CGRP-targeted therapy is listed as one of the first-line treatment options for both episodic and chronic migraine prevention. A history of failure of multiple preventive medications is not required before initiating CGRP-targeted therapy, as early initiation may provide better migraine control than delayed treatment. For both episodic and chronic migraine, the Taiwan Headache Society recommends that CGRP-targeted therapy may be continued for up to 12 months. This update is crucial for improving migraine care and highlights the importance of continuous CGRP-targeted therapy, rather than premature or unnecessary treatment interruption.

title: Mosaic CDKL5 deficiency drives progressive inhibitory circuit remodelling.
abstract: CDKL5 deficiency disorder predominantly affects heterozygous females, in whom random X-chromosome inactivation generates cellular CDKL5 mosaicism. Although mosaicism is a defining feature of the disease, whether it actively drives disease progression or simply reflects the genetic mode of inheritance remains unknown. Here, we combined age-comparative electrophysiology, quantitative synaptic imaging, transcriptomic profiling and postmortem human brain analyses to determine how mosaic CDKL5 deficiency shapes inhibitory circuit remodeling during disease progression. Heterozygous Cdkl5 female mice exhibited striking age- and region-specific remodeling of inhibitory neurotransmission. Hippocampal inhibition was initially enhanced but progressively declined with age, whereas cortical inhibitory transmission remained preserved at 3 months and increased in middle-aged animals. These functional changes were accompanied by dynamic remodeling of inhibitory presynaptic terminals, persistent disruption of inhibitory synapse organization and reduced hippocampal gephyrin-positive puncta despite preservation of the major inhibitory interneuron populations. At 12 months, heterozygous females also exhibited a higher density of IBA1/CD68 double-positive microglia in both regions compared with age-matched wild-type controls. Importantly, complete Cdkl5 deficiency failed to reproduce the progressive loss of inhibitory presynaptic terminals observed in heterozygous females, indicating that this phenotype is specific to the mosaic condition rather than a simple consequence of complete Cdkl5 loss. Transcriptomic profiling revealed a temporal transition from alterations detected at 3 months in immune-synaptic regulatory pathways to activity-dependent transcriptional programs associated with reduced structural and homeostatic support, consistent with progressive hippocampal circuit reorganization. Exploratory analyses of postmortem cortical tissue from individuals with CDD revealed differences in inhibitory presynaptic labeling between the available young and adult cases, suggesting that inhibitory alterations may also vary with age in human CDD. Together, these findings identify mosaic CDKL5 deficiency as a biologically distinct circuit state characterized by progressive, region-specific inhibitory circuit remodeling and provide a mechanistic framework for disease progression in CDKL5 deficiency disorder.

title: Neuronal cell-cycle re-entry stratifies clinical trajectories in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.
abstract: The clinical heterogeneity of Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS) remains a fundamental barrier to effective therapy. While cell cycle re-entry in post-mitotic neurons is a known precursor to neurodegeneration, its role in defining patient-specific outcomes has never been established. Here, we integrate large-scale transcriptomic profiling from the AnswerALS cohort with mechanistic studies in human iPSC-derived spinal motor neurons to define how cell-cycle re-entry shapes disease heterogeneity in ALS. We identify a transcriptionally distinct patient subgroup with the highest expression of G1 or G2-phase cyclins that exhibit significantly slower functional decline (ALSFRS-R), whereas the engagement of S-phase markers correlates with accelerated disease progression. Nucleocytoplasmic transport dysfunction, a hallmark of ALS and related disorders, disrupts the spatial distribution of key regulatory proteins and may contribute to maladaptive cell-cycle activation. Our recent evidence suggests that impaired nuclear import may initiate, rather than merely accompany, neuronal cell-cycle re-entry. Using iPSC-derived motor neurons, we show that impaired nuclear import initiates TDP-43 pathology and global nuclear/cytoplasmic mis-localization of key ALS-related proteins. This nucleocytoplasmic transport dysfunction triggers a transient wave of cell-cycle activity immediately preceding neuronal cell death. Crucially, we show that DNA-replication initiation is a pathological inflection point of no return, as neurons entering S-phase accumulate replication-associated DNA damage and undergo cell death. Selective inhibition of CDK4/6 prevents S-phase entry and confers potent neuroprotection. Our findings demonstrate that impaired nuclear import drives maladaptive cell-cycle reactivation in ALS and that the depth of cell-cycle engagement stratifies neuronal fate and patient trajectories.

title: Reply: Reading between the blinks: how much can prepulse inhibition tell us about fibromyalgia?
Reading between the blinks: how much can prepulse inhibition tell us about fibromyalgia?
Personalised community based telerehabilitation post stroke to increase rehabilitation time and improve motor recovery (PRACTISE): study protocol for a randomised controlled feasibility trial.
abstract: Stroke is the second leading non-communicable cause of death and third leading cause of death and disability worldwide with prevalence expected to rise 120% between 2015 and 2035. The first 6 months after stroke is the optimum time for neuroplasticity and a critical period for rehabilitation. UK national clinical guidelines recommend stroke survivors should receive at least 3 h/day of multidisciplinary rehabilitation at least 5 days/week. Workforce shortages and service variability make achieving this standard consistently challenging. Goal setting, telerehabilitation, and self-management strategies are advocated, yet their combined use in community-based rehabilitation has not been tested. This study aims to conduct a randomised feasibility-controlled trial with embedded process evaluation to assess the feasibility of delivering a 16-week, personalised, home-based physiotherapy, prior to progression to a full-scale trial. This trial will recruit 60 participants with moderate post-stroke disability across Scotland. Participants will be randomised to the PRACTISE intervention or control (usual physiotherapy). PRACTISE (Personalised community-based telerehabilitation post stroke to increase rehabilitation time and improve motor recovery) is a 16-week, personalised physiotherapy programme involving goal setting, supported self-management and exercise via an online video-based platform. PRACTISE consists of five home-based physiotherapy sessions and four online/telephone sessions with participants encouraged to engage in a personalised exercise programme up to five times/week for up to 3 h/day. Both groups will receive other usual stroke care. Feasibility outcomes will include recruitment, retention, and completion rates. A process evaluation will assess acceptability and implementation factors. Clinical outcomes, recorded at weeks 0, 8, 16, and 24 by a blinded assessor, include the Canadian Occupational Performance Measure (primary outcome) and measures of limb function, fatigue, quality of life, functional ability, treatment burden, falls, self-efficacy, caregiver strain, and healthcare resource use (secondary outcomes). Exercise dosage and adherence will be monitored via exercise diaries. Intensive post-stroke rehabilitation is recommended but challenging to achieve. PRACTISE combines goal setting, self-management, and online exercise prescription to support stroke survivors to achieve recommended rehabilitation doses. This study will examine the feasibility, acceptability, and mechanisms of the intervention to inform potential refinement and progression to a full-scale trial. Prospectively registered at https://clinicaltrials.gov . (NCT06871878).

title: A synergistic strategy of subacute scar tissue resection and paclitaxel-loaded fibrin scaffold grafting for spinal cord injury repair.
abstract: Scar tissue impede axonal regeneration and hinder functional recovery after spinal cord injury. Previous studies have demonstrated excision of scar tissue during the subacute phase (particularly on day 10) not only enhances neuronal regeneration but also identifies microtubule stabilization as a key contributor to axonal regeneration in this process. Here we grafted fibrin scaffolds loaded with paclitaxel (a microtubule-stabilizing agent) immediately after scar excision during subacute stage, with the aim of stabilizing axonal microtubules. Our results showed that paclitaxel promoted functional recovery of injured rats by enhancing neuronal regeneration and axonal elongation post resecting scars in subacute stage. In paclitaxel-fibrin-grafted group, the microenvironment post injury was significantly improved. The secretion of pro-regenerative factors (laminin, BDNF and NT-3) was upregulated and the deposition of CSPG, a key inhibitory component of the scar tissue, was reduced in injured spinal tissue under paclitaxel-fibrin. Moreover, BSCB (blood spinal cord barrier) was reconstructed that alleviated the continuous infiltration of immune cells into the lesion site. Collectively, these findings suggest that the administration of paclitaxel following scar resection during subacute stage may hold significant potential in the treatment of SCI.

title: Gut microbiota heterogeneity is linked to social dysfunction in severe alcohol use disorder.
abstract: Gut microbiota and social functioning are both substantially altered in individuals with severe alcohol use disorder (sAUD). However, it remains unclear whether inter-individual variability in gut microbiota composition identifies biologically and clinically distinct subgroups of patients, particularly in relation to social functioning. Based on previous investigations of gut-brain axis interactions in autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and other psychiatric disorders, we investigated whether gut microbiota-based stratification is associated with differences in social functioning and biological profiles in sAUD. The social dimension is crucial for relapse risk after detoxification. Forty-six sAUD patients undergoing detoxification were stratified into dysbiotic and non-dysbiotic subgroups based on gut microbiota β-diversity. Bray-Curtis distances were computed and principal coordinate analysis performed. Patients were classified as dysbiotic when their first-axis score deviated > 1.65 standard deviations from the healthy subjects (HS) distribution. Groups were compared with HS in a cross-sectional design. Metabolomic profiles, inflammatory markers, dietary habits, psychological symptoms, and social functioning were compared. We applied a comprehensive assessment of social functioning combining sociodemographic data, an emotional intelligence questionnaire, a social cognition task and personal social networks (evaluated through mapping techniques). One third of the sAUD patients exhibited microbial alterations. The non-dysbiotic subgroup showed an overall microbial composition more similar to HS than the dysbiotic subgroup. The dysbiotic patients were younger, leaner, and reported higher alcohol craving compared to the non-dysbiotic patients. The dysbiotic subgroup also displayed altered metabolomic and nutritional profiles and a higher plasma IL-8 level. Interestingly, we observed a coherent profile of severe impairments across social functioning indexes in the dysbiotic group: they had lower sociability scores, displayed impairment in social cognition (with greater difficulty in spontaneously considering another's perspective), were more often divorced/separated and unemployed, and had a smaller, less cohesive, and less diverse personal social network compared to the non-dysbiotic group. We found a significant relationship between gut dysbiosis and various aspects of social functioning in sAUD. These findings are associative and do not establish causality, but suggest that targeting the gut microbiota could offer a novel approach to address social impairments in sAUD. Video Abstract.

title: Disentangling the role of adaptive immunity in Alzheimer's disease.
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD), the most common age-related neurodegenerative disorder, is characterized by progressive synaptic and neuronal loss, amyloid-β deposition, hyperphosphorylated tau accumulation, and chronic neuroinflammation, traditionally attributed primarily to the innate immune system. Increasing evidence, however, implicates the adaptive immune system as an active contributor to AD pathogenesis and progression. This emerging perspective has stimulated the development of immunomodulatory strategies aimed at mitigating cognitive decline and neuropathological hallmarks of the disease. In this review, we examine how adaptive immune responses change throughout the course of AD, integrating findings from both human studies and animal models while emphasizing the temporal dynamics of these alterations. We critically evaluate areas of consensus and controversy in the field, highlighting how differences in experimental models, disease stages, and methodological approaches contribute to divergent findings. Finally, we assess current therapeutic strategies targeting adaptive immunity, discussing their potential mechanisms of action and identifying key therapeutic windows and routes of administration that may maximize efficacy. By providing a comprehensive overview of adaptive immune involvement in AD, this review aims to inform the development of more precise and effective immunomodulatory interventions.

title: An ex vivo gut mucosal explant assay to compare HIV tissue susceptibility shows increased HIV susceptibility with methamphetamine exposure.
abstract: Existing ex vivo mucosal explant models for HIV assess viral replication but do not fully capture the ability of tissue to support productive infection and transfer to target cells, an important indicator of tissue susceptibility. Additional tools to investigate relative mucosal susceptibility to HIV are necessary to better understand risk factors, such as substance use, or to evaluate therapeutics. We developed an ex vivo gut mucosal explant assay incorporating a CCR5/CXCR4-expressing GFP-indicator cell co-culture to quantify both viral replication and transfer. Susceptibility was quantified using a composite metric based on time to infection endpoint across viral doses. Modulators of susceptibility, including anti-CD3 stimulation, tenofovir, and methamphetamine, were evaluated. The assay reliably detected differences in tissue susceptibility under various experimental conditions. We detected enhanced susceptibility following anti-CD3 stimulation, while tenofovir pretreatment reduced susceptibility in a dose-dependent manner. Methamphetamine exposure resulted in a modest but significant increase in gut tissue susceptibility to HIV. This novel ex vivo explant susceptibility assay advances HIV mucosal transmission research by measuring both viral production and transfer. It can detect subtle changes in susceptibility, providing a versatile platform for evaluating prevention therapeutics, host and microbial factors, and substance use effects.

title: Vessels supplying blood to the encephalon of the alpaca (Vicugna pacos).
abstract: Studies on the blood vessels of the brain in Cameliformes have largely focused on Old World camels, with limited data on New World species such as alpacas. The rostral epidural rete mirabile, a specialized arterial network at the base of the brain, plays a role in brain cooling, water conservation, and neurotransmitter transport in other ungulates. Alpacas are increasingly bred in Europe yet detailed anatomical descriptions of their cerebral arteries and the rostral epidural rete mirabile are lacking. This study aimed to analyze the blood supply to the encephalon in alpacas, with a focus on the rostral epidural rete mirabile, to provide insights relevant for anatomy, physiology, and veterinary care. The internal carotid artery enters the rostral epidural rete mirabile from the caudal side, accompanied by branches from the maxillary and external ophthalmic arteries. The paired rete is well-developed, located on the basal sphenoid bone, with 51-64 interconnecting vessels forming an elongated oval structure. Blood from the rete supplies the cerebral arterial circle, including the rostral cerebral artery and caudal communicating arteries. The rostral cerebral arteries are connected rostrally by the rostral communicating artery in most specimens. The caudal cerebral and cerebellar arteries, along with the basilar artery, supply the posterior cerebrum, brainstem, and cerebellum. Variations were observed in the presence and branching patterns of certain arteries, including unilateral or bilateral absence of caudal branches. The rete is embedded in the cavernous sinus, which has a spongy structure due to interspersed arterial vessels. In alpacas, the brain is supplied by the internal carotid artery, the rostral and caudal branches to the rostral epidural rete mirabile, and the basilar artery. The vascular pattern remains constant during ontogenesis, with the internal carotid artery preserved in adults. The rostral epidural rete mirabile is well developed, especially in its rostral part, and embedded within the cavernous sinus. The cerebral arterial circle is formed by the rostral cerebral and caudal communicating arteries. The basilar artery plays a key role in maintaining adequate blood flow to the brain.

title: Ethionamide preconditioning enhances the therapeutic efficacy of human mesenchymal stromal cells in an Alzheimer's disease model.
abstract: Mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) are promising therapeutic candidates for neurodegenerative diseases, including Alzheimer's disease (AD). However, their limited survival and functionality in pathological environments hinder their therapeutic efficacy. The primary objective of this study was to evaluate the therapeutic efficacy of ethionamide (ETH)-preconditioned MSCs (ETH-MSCs) in mitigating AD pathology. Wharton's jelly-derived MSCs (WJ-MSCs) were preconditioned with ethionamide, and their therapeutic efficacy was evaluated in both in vitro and in vivo AD models. In vitro, ETH-MSCs were assessed for their ability to modulate microglial inflammation and promote amyloid-β (Aβ) clearance under AD-like conditions. For in vivo studies, ETH-MSCs were injected into the lateral ventricles of 5xFAD transgenic mice. The effects of ETH-MSC administration on glial activation (GFAP and Iba1 expression) and Aβ deposition were evaluated. In vitro, ETH-MSCs reduced pro-inflammatory cytokine secretion by microglia and enhanced Aβ clearance in neurons. In vivo, ETH-MSCs treatment significantly decreased GFAP and Iba1 expression, indicating reduced astroglial and microglial activation, and reduced amyloid plaque burden in 5xFAD mice. Repeated ETH-MSCs injections further boosted Aβ clearance, demonstrating a cumulative therapeutic benefit. Ethionamide preconditioning significantly enhances the neuroprotective and amyloid-clearing capabilities of WJ-MSCs. These findings suggest the potential of ETH-MSCs as an effective therapeutic strategy for AD, with superior efficacy compared to naïve MSCs in both in vitro and in vivo models.

title: Motor imagery enhances swallowing motor cortex excitability and activates sensorimotor regions: a TMS and fNIRS study.
abstract: Action observation (AO) and motor imagery (MI) represent promising, non-invasive strategies for promoting neuroplasticity in motor rehabilitation by engaging the shared neural substrates of actual movement. However, their translation to swallowing rehabilitation, particularly for neurogenic dysphagia, lacks a robust neurophysiological foundation. A critical barrier is the absence of direct, multimodal evidence comparing how swallowing-specific static AO (SAO), dynamic AO (DAO), and MI differentially engage the cortical swallowing network. Specifically, their immediate effects on corticobulbar excitability and hemodynamic activation within key sensorimotor regions remain unquantified and poorly contrasted, limiting the rationale for their targeted clinical application. This study employed a dual-modal neuroimaging approach to precisely quantify and compare the immediate neurophysiological effects of SAO, DAO, and MI on the human swallowing sensorimotor system. We aim to evaluate their modulatory effects on bilateral suprahyoid motor cortical excitability and intracortical inhibitory/facilitatory circuitry using transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS), and map their hemodynamic activation patterns within core sensorimotor cortices compared to motor execution (ME) using functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS). Thirty-two healthy adults underwent integrated assessments using transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) and functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS). TMS measured motor-evoked potentials (MEPs), short-interval intracortical inhibition (SICI), and intracortical facilitation (ICF) in bilateral suprahyoid motor cortices during rest, SAO, DAO, and MI. fNIRS mapped hemodynamic changes in dorsal/ventral precentral (dPreCG/vPreCG) and postcentral gyri (dPoCG/vPoCG), superior/middle frontal gyri (SFG/MFG) during swallowing-specific SAO, DAO, MI and ME. MI reduced bilateral SICI and increased left ICF, concurrently activating bilateral dPoCG, left SFG/MFG, and right dPreCG/vPreCG/vPoCG-regions overlapping with ME-activated networks (bilateral vPreCG/vPoCG/MFG), with left MFG, right vPreCG/vPoCG as coactivating areas. In contrast, DAO reduced left SICI but elicited no hemodynamic activation, while SAO showed no significant effects. MI enhances the excitability of the swallowing motor cortex and activates the key sensorimotor cortical areas governed ME of swallowing. MI shows greater superiority over AO and may become a promising effective rehabilitation strategy for neurogenic dysphagia. Trial registration Chinese Clinical Trial Registry, ChiCTR2000036715. Registered on 24 August 2020, https//www.chictr.org.cn/bin/home.

title: Obturator hernia as a cause of small bowel obstruction in an 80-year-old female patient with comorbidities: management and challenges in a resource-limited setting: a case report.
abstract: Obturator hernia is one of the rarest types of hernia and accounts for only a small percentage of small bowel obstructions. It may be asymptomatic, but most patients present with acute intestinal obstruction. Some patients may also report pain along the medial aspect of the thigh due to compression of the obturator nerve. The clinical presentation of obturator hernia is often non-specific, which makes diagnosis challenging. Imaging modalities such as ultrasonography, herniography, and computed tomography (CT) of the abdomen can aid in diagnosis. Although non-surgical management has been described in the literature, it is frequently associated with high morbidity and mortality. Surgical intervention remains the treatment of choice. An 80-year-old female patient presented with crampy periumbilical abdominal pain of one week's duration. She also reported one to two episodes of vomiting per day for five days, consisting of ingested material, associated with failure to pass feces and flatus. She had progressive abdominal distension for four days. Further history revealed a two-week history of high-grade intermittent fever and productive cough with whitish sputum. On examination, she was in severe abdominal pain and tachycardic, with a pulse rate of 124 beats per minute and an irregularly irregular rhythm. Abdominal examination revealed visible peristalsis. Investigations, including serology and radiologic imaging, were performed. Plain abdominal radiography showed signs of small bowel obstruction, while chest X-ray revealed pneumonia. Electrocardiography demonstrated atrial fibrillation, and echocardiography showed valvular degeneration. The findings were discussed with the patient and her family, and they opted for surgical intervention. After obtaining informed consent, laparotomy was performed. Intraoperatively, a small bowel loop approximately 50 cm from the ileocecal valve was found herniated through the obturator foramen. A 1 × 2 cm defect was noted on the antimesenteric side of the herniated bowel segment. Repair and anastomosis were performed, and the patient left the operating room with stable vital signs. She remained hospitalized for six days postoperatively and was subsequently discharged with outpatient follow-up. Follow-up visits were uneventful, with significant clinical improvement. Although obturator hernia is a rare cause of small bowel obstruction, it should be considered in the differential diagnosis of elderly female patients. Maintaining a high index of suspicion facilitates early diagnosis and timely management, as delayed recognition is associated with increased morbidity and mortality.

title: Exhaled nitric oxide amplification via functionalized vesicles enables non-invasive diagnosis of pulmonary infection.
abstract: Pulmonary infections remain difficult to diagnose rapidly and non-invasively, as existing biomarkers lack both sensitivity and specificity. Here we present functionalized biomarker vesicles (FBVs), an inhalable nanotechnology platform that amplifies fractional exhaled nitric oxide (FeNO) in an infection-specific manner. FBVs are engineered from inactivated bacterial membranes and encapsulate L-arginine and NADPH, enabling selective uptake by M1-polarized macrophages within infected lung tissue. Upon phagocytosis or membrane fusion with iNOS-containing vesicles, FBVs release their payload to drive localized nitric oxide production, directly linking FeNO amplification to pathogen-induced immune activation. Optimized FBVs (800 nm) demonstrated efficient pulmonary delivery, robust macrophage uptake, and NO output tightly correlated with iNOS expression. In mouse infection models, FBV-induced FeNO distinguished infected from healthy with high accuracy (AUC = 0.94). In clinical bronchoalveolar lavage samples, FBV-based detection outperformed extracellular vesicle quantification, achieving superior diagnostic performance (AUC = 0.93). This strategy establishes a non-invasive diagnostic modality that couples host immune activation to measurable breath biomarkers, providing a direct path toward clinical translation for respiratory infection management.

title: Prohibitin 1 orchestrates mitochondrial-ER crosstalk via the VDAC1-GRP75-IP3R axis to drive malignancy in gastric cancer.
abstract: Mitochondria-associated endoplasmic reticulum (ER) membranes (MAMs), serving as critical hubs for mitochondrial-ER interactions, play a pivotal role in cancer progression. Prohibitin 1 (PHB1), an inner mitochondrial membrane protein, contributes to tumorigenesis by regulating energy metabolism and structural integrity. This study aimed to explore the association between PHB1 and MAMs structural integrity, as well as the downstream signaling potentially involved in gastric cancer (GC) metastasis. We analyzed the expression profiles of PHB1/PHB2 in GC tissue using the TCGA database. Immunohistochemistry was performed to detect PHB1/PHB2 protein expression in GC tissues, normal gastric tissues, and greater omental metastasis tissues, and to assess their correlation with clinicopathological features. Immunofluorescence and proximity ligation assay (PLA) were used to observe the co-localization of PHB1 with the IP3R-GRP75-VDAC1 complex. Live-cell Ca2+ imaging, ATP/ROS detection, and mitochondrial functional assays (mPTP opening/MMP) were employed to evaluate calcium flux and energy metabolism changes. Transmission electron microscopy and Western blot were utilized to analyze MAMs structural integrity. The specific VDAC1 inhibitor VBIT-12 and the calcium chelator BAPTA-AM were used to validate the VDAC1-GRP75-IP3R signaling axis and the causal relationship between PHB1-dependent MAMs signalling and the downstream cellular phenotypes. A nude mouse xenograft model was established to validate in vivo functions. TCGA analysis confirmed that both PHB1 and PHB2 were overexpressed in GC tissue. PHB1 expression significantly correlated with tumor stage, while PHB2 expression correlated with demographic characteristics. Moreover, the expression of PHB1 was significantly higher than that of PHB2 in omental metastasis tissues. PHB1 overexpression enhanced its co-localization and interaction with the IP3R-GRP75-VDAC1 complex, thereby regulating Ca2+ flux from the ER to mitochondria. In addition, PHB1 overexpression increased ATP production, and drove cytoskeletal remodeling, thereby promoting malignant progression. Conversely, PHB1 knockdown disrupted the IP3R-GRP75-VDAC1 axis, leading to MAMs structural dissociation and mitochondrial dysfunction. Furthermore, BAPTA-AM blocked the OE-PHB1-induced enhancement of CDC42 expression, cytoskeletal remodeling. Notably, treatment with VBIT-12 in PHB1-overexpressing cells significantly reversed the pro-tumorigenic effects of PHB1, reduced PHB1 protein levels, and diminished its association with the GRP75-IP3R complex, suggesting that VDAC1 integrity is critical for PHB1-mediated effects. In summary, PHB1 is associated with MAMs structural integrity and functionally coupled to the VDAC1-GRP75-IP3R complex in a VDAC1-integrity-associated manner. This subsequently modulates calcium homeostasis, mitochondrial energy metabolism, and cytoskeletal remodeling, ultimately driving GC progression. These findings suggest a novel mechanism by which PHB1 may promote GC progression through its association with MAMs function involving the VDAC1 complex, providing a theoretical basis for further investigation of therapeutic targeting.

title: Daily patterns and prevalence of behavioral and psychological symptoms of dementia in Swedish nursing homes.
abstract: Behavioral and psychological symptoms of dementia (BPSD) are among the principal observable expressions of psychological distress and unmet need in nursing home residents who can no longer reliably verbalize internal experiences, and recognizing their day-to-day variation underpins timely, person-centered care. Yet BPSD fluctuate across days, shifts, and contexts, while established instruments such as the Neuropsychiatric Inventory Nursing Home version (NPI-NH) assess them retrospectively over the preceding weeks or months. This mismatch leaves basic descriptive questions about the day-to-day symptom landscape in routine care unanswered. This study describes the prevalence, severity, co-occurrence, between-unit variation, and shift and weekday patterns of BPSD documented through structured daily registrations in nursing home care. Descriptive longitudinal observational study of 230 individuals with dementia in six nursing homes across six Swedish municipalities, followed for a median observation period of 270 days (interquartile range 120 to 446). Care staff used a digital tool to rate the severity (0-3) of twelve common BPSD, adapted from the NPI-NH, at the end of every work shift, yielding over one million symptom registrations. Analyses were descriptive and person-weighted, giving each individual equal weight regardless of observation length. Cumulative symptom prevalence (at any point during observation) ranged from 90% (agitation) to 70% (euphoria). Each symptom's mean daily prevalence was much lower (4-18%), and symptoms were predominantly of low severity. At least one symptom was recorded on a median of 43.5% of registered days, varying widely between individuals. Clinically related symptoms tended to occur together, consistent with established NPI-NH domain structures, and the mean number of symptoms per day varied more than twofold across the six units. Symptoms were most frequent on evening shifts and least frequent at night, except sleep disturbances, with little variation across weekdays. Just under half of all possible shift registrations were completed. Daily registrations describe an intermittent and heterogeneous symptom landscape at a resolution that periodic assessments are not designed to provide. These findings provide an empirical baseline for future multilevel analyses and support BPSD monitoring that covers both individual symptoms and the daily number of symptoms in nursing homes. Not applicable.

title: Dynamic cerebral autoregulation and exercise-induced neurovascular coupling as potential markers of cerebral hyperperfusion after carotid stenting.
abstract: This study aimed to prospectively evaluate whether impaired dynamic cerebral autoregulation (dCA) and exercise-induced neurovascular coupling (NVC) parameters in carotid stenosis predict cerebral hyperperfusion (CH) after carotid artery stenting (CAS). This study was conducted based on prospectively collected data from a single-center observational registry. Between October 2023 and September 2024, the registry enrolled 237 patients scheduled to undergo CAS, all with carotid artery stenosis (≥ 70% for asymptomatic or ≥ 50% for symptomatic stenosis). To assess NVC, transcranial Doppler (TCD) was performed within 24 h prior to CAS. NVC was evaluated by measuring the increase in cerebral blood velocity (CBv) in the middle cerebral artery (MCA) during stimulation. Ultimately, 93 patients proceeded to stenting and were included in the present analysis. Among 93 patients undergoing CAS, 16.1% (n = 15) developed CH. These patients exhibited significantly lower phase values in very low frequency (VLF) compared to non-CH patients during exercise (23.12° vs. 41.82°, p < 0.05). NVC was compromised in CH patients, demonstrated by reduced exercise-induced flow response (EIFR) (5.6% vs. 8.6%, p = 0.041) and Δcerebrovascular conductance index (ΔCVCi) (p = 0.015). The hemodynamic and regulatory model integrating phase at VLF, ΔCVCi, and EIFR showed a higher AUC compared with the clinical model, though the difference did not reach statistical significance (p = 0.20). This study suggests that dCA and NVC parameters during exercise stimulation may serve as potential predictors of CH after CAS, supporting further investigation of cerebrovascular autoregulation assessment in preoperative evaluation for carotid revascularization.

title: Neuregulin 2 and tubulin protein levels in children with autism spectrum disorder.
abstract: Multiple lines of evidence suggest that neuregulin 2 (NRG2) and tubulin play important roles in the neuron cytoskeleton, neuronal development, synaptic plasticity, and downstream signaling pathways implicated in autism spectrum disorder (ASD). This study aimed to investigate plasma levels of NRG2 and tubulin in ASD and to examine their association with the ASD severity and social impairment. Plasma levels of NRG2 and tubulin were measured using a sandwich enzyme immunoassay in 40 children with ASD and 40 age-matched healthy controls. Autism severity and social impairment were evaluated by the childhood autism rating scale (CARS) and Social Responsiveness Scale (SRS) respectively. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was performed to determine the area under the curve (AUC), and Spearman's correlation coefficients (r) were calculated to examine the relationships between NRG2 and tubulin levels and CARS, SRS, and age using SPSS. Significantly decreased plasma levels of NRG2 were observed in children with ASD (n = 40, 4.27 ± 0.26 ng/ml [mean ± SEM]) compared with healthy controls (n = 40, 5.44 ± 0.42 ng/ml, [mean ± SEM], p < 0.05). Similarly, plasma tubulin levels were significantly lower in children with ASD (n = 37, 3.65 ± 0.42 ng /ml) than in healthy controls (n = 38, 6.05 ± 0.48 ng /ml), [mean ± SEM], p < 0.05). Segregation of children with ASD into ASD level 2 and ASD level 3 autism revealed that both the ASD level 2 (n = 17, 3.03 ± 0.40 ng /ml, p = 0.001) and ASD level 3 group (n = 20, 4.18 ± 0.57 ng /ml p = 0.01) had significantly lower tubulin levels (p < 0.05), compared with control children. NRG2 was significantly positively correlated with SRS scores (r = 0.434, p = 0.005), whereas tubulin exhibited significant diagnostic accuracy (AUC = 0.743, 95% CI [0.146-0.369], p < 0.001). Our findings highlight the potential involvement of NRG2 and tubulin in the pathophysiology of ASD, particularly in relation to neuronal development and synaptic function. Their association with social ability of children with ASD and diagnostic sensitivity suggests that they may serve as promising candidate biomarkers. Further large-scale studies are needed to confirm these findings and clarify their roles in ASD pathogenesis.

title: Clinical characterization in a population of latin-American older adults using the frontotemporal dementia assessment scale: an observational study.
abstract: Aging is associated with gradual changes in cognitive, functional, and behavioral domains that may affect everyday functioning in older adults. In Latin America, these these functional and behavioral variations are frequently underrecognized in community settings due to limited access to standardized assessment tools. The Frontotemporal Dementia Rating Scale (FTD-FRS), validated in Spanish, allows allows the assessment of functional and behavioral changes related to daily activities and executive functioning beyond clinically diagnosed dementia. This study aimed to examine the presence and distribution of these changes in adults over 65 years participating in healthy aging programs in Bogotá, Colombia. This cross-sectional observational study was conducted among 80 adults aged 65 years or older who participated in community programs for healthy aging in Bogotá, Colombia. Individuals with a current diagnosis of cognitive impairment, dementia, or psychiatric disorders were excluded, and after providing written informed consent, the FTD-FRS, The FTD-FRS, consisting of 30 items that classify participants into six preservation categories, was administered. A descriptive analysis of the results was performed, while the associations between FTD-FRS preservation scores and sociodemographic variables were explored using JASP version 0.95.4. Most participants showed variability in functional performance according to the FTD-FRS, with only 28.75% classified as normal/very mild, while the mild preservation category was the most prevalent in the population (41.25%). The domains "self-care and mobility" and "food preparation and consumption" were preserved in 93.1% and 89.5% of the population, respectively, while 'behavior' and 'medication management' showed the lowest preservation scores (75.5% each). Additionally, a trend toward lower FTD-FRS preservation scores was observed in participants with lower educational and socioeconomic levels, although without statistically significant differences. The application of the FTD-FRS in a population of community-dwelling older adults considered healthy and functionally independent demonstrated variability in functional performance across several domains of everyday functioning. Within the context of this exploratory study, the FTD-FRS proved to be a useful and accessible instrument for the descriptive characterization of functional performance. Future studies incorporating complementary cognitive, neuropsychological, and longitudinal assessments are needed to further evaluate its application in community settings.

title: A systematic review of telemedicine for stroke in South-East Asia Region.
abstract: Telestroke is an innovation in telemedicine in the form of a method for identifying, assessing, treating and monitoring stroke patients remotely using internet technology. Telestroke can speed up the diagnosis and treatment of acute stroke through direct video consultations between doctors and patients separated by distance. The aim of this systematic review is to analyze the implementation of telestroke in improving the clinical outcomes of acute stroke patients in the South-East Asia Region (SEAR). The literature search was carried out through 2 electronic databases, namely PubMed and ScienceDirect which include articles published up to 31 December 2024, and published in English. Before selecting the studies, the study duplication was detected by Zotero Reference Manager® and then removed. The related studies examined and selected with rayyan.ai® website using a "blind-on" mode to ensure eligibility. A total of 6 studies were included. We found that there were 3 types of telestroke programs being implemented, namely remote radiology teleconsultation, drip and ship methods, and also international teleconsultation between Thailand and Laos. Telestroke can provide better opportunities and associated with the clinical outcomes of acute stroke patients with faster door-to-treatment and better 3-month outcomes as well, although published data is still limited. It is hoped that telestroke can bridge this gap, allowing hospitals in rural areas to provide care equivalent to hospitals that have stroke specialists especially in SEAR for improving acute stroke services.

title: Is the effect of sex on post-thrombectomy outcomes in acute ischemic stroke age-dependent? Results from an international prospective registry (EVA-TRISP).
abstract: We aimed to investigate the effect of sex on clinical outcomes after endovascular treatment (EVT) in ischemic stroke patients and whether this effect is age dependent. We used data from EVA-TRISP, a multicentre registry of consecutive EVT patients. Primary outcome was the 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score, analysed with unadjusted and adjusted mixed model ordinal regression. We compared women with men and assessed the interaction between age and sex. We assessed age both as a continuous variable and dichotomized at the population median. In total, 12,915 EVT patients were included for the current study (median age 74 [IQR 64-82] years, 6,251 [48.4%] women). Female patients were older (77 [IQR 67-84] vs 72 [IQR: 62-80], p < 0.001) and had a higher median baseline NIHSS (15 [IQR 9-19] vs 14 [IQR 8-19], p < 0.001). Female sex was associated with worse functional outcome in the unadjusted analysis (cOR 1.22, 95%CI:1.14-1.29) but not in the adjusted analysis (acOR 1.02, 95%CI:0.95-1.09). We found no significant interaction between age and sex when assessing age as a continuous variable (p = 0.08), but observed a significant interaction when dichotomizing age (p = 0.01). In patients aged 74 or younger, women had worse outcomes than men (acOR 1.10, 95%CI:1.003-1.20) while sex was not associated with functional outcome in older patients (acOR 0.93, 95%CI:0.85-1.02). We did not find clear evidence that the effect of sex on post-EVT outcomes is modified by age when using age as continuous variable, but observed a worse outcome in women in patients aged 74 or younger.

title: Degradation-Driven Implications for the Pharmacology and Risk Profile of Fexofenadine.
abstract: Understanding a drug's degradation profile is essential for ensuring its stability, efficacy, and safety. This minireview summarizes the pharmacological characteristics of fexofenadine and predicts its degradation pathways, with an emphasis on quality assessment and regulatory implications. To build on the outlined objectives, a systematic search was conducted in PubMed and Scopus using keywords related to fexofenadine's pharmacology, chemical structure, and degradation mechanisms. Of 368 records identified, 52 studies met the inclusion criteria and were critically analyzed. Following this analysis, it was found that fexofenadine is susceptible to photolysis, hydrolysis, and N-nitrosation processes. Fexofenadine's vulnerabilities, which are corroborated by forced degradation studies, may compromise its stability and lead to nitrosamine formation. Notably, the drug is primarily excreted unchanged, indicating minimal metabolic transformation. Predicted metabolic routes include aromatic hydroxylation, Ndealkylation, and piperidine ring opening; however, its high polarity favors renal elimination. Phase II conjugation, particularly glucuronidation, may further contribute to its clearance and the absence of detectable metabolites. In addition, nanoformulations have been shown to enhance fexofenadine's stability, bioavailability, and therapeutic performance. Further investigation into fexofenadine's stability is critical for optimizing formulation strategies, guiding quality control, and mitigating degradation-related risks. Theoretical and experimental insights can strengthen regulatory compliance and ensure sustained drug safety.

title: The SaeRS two-component system likely mediates the major dopamine-dependent regulation of virulence in Staphylococcus aureus ATCC 25,923.
abstract: Staphylococcus aureus(S. aureus)is an important foodborne pathogen. Host-derived catecholamines released under stress are known to influence bacterial pathogenic processes, including growth, virulence, biofilm formation. However, the role of dopamine in this context remains less well understood, particularly in S. aureus.
